badge.title: badge
badge.text: A simple badge element that can be used to indicate status or convey simple messages. <moz-badge label="New" type="new"></moz-badge> label Text to display on the badge, by default inferred from type (falls back to a fluent id per type when unset). iconSrc The src for an optional icon shown next to the label. title The title of the badge, appears as a tooltip on hover. type The type of badge. Leave label empty if you want the built-in Fluent text, since labelL10nId only supplies "moz-badge-beta2"/"moz-badge-new2" strings for type="beta"/"new" when there is no explicit label to override it. Don't expect the title attribute to behave like a normal reflected tooltip afterward, MozLitElement's mapped-attribute handling moves it into an internal titleAttribute and clears the host attribute the first time it's set, and per lit-utils.mjs's own comment the attribute can not be unset once it is set. moz-badge.background.color.@base moz-badge.background.color.filled moz-badge.border.color.@base moz-badge.border.color.filled moz-badge.border.radius moz-badge.border.width moz-badge.font.weight moz-badge.padding.block moz-badge.padding.inline moz-badge.text.color.@base moz-badge.text.color.filled

bookmarks-toolbar.title: bookmarks-toolbar
bookmarks-toolbar.text: PlacesToolbar (extends PlacesViewBase) is a plain JS view class, not a custom element. **Manually instantiated, not self-registering:** browser-places.js constructs it as `new PlacesToolbar(...)` against the existing #PlacesToolbarItems/#PersonalToolbar markup and attaches it as `_placesView`. **What it handles:** rendering, drag-and-drop, overflow chevron, and resize behavior for the bookmarks toolbar. Instantiate PlacesToolbar directly against the real #PlacesToolbarItems/#PersonalToolbar markup already in the document, it's manually constructed (new PlacesToolbar(...)) by browser-places.js, not something that self-initializes from a custom element. Don't look elsewhere for drag-and-drop, the overflow chevron, or resize handling, PlacesToolbar (extends PlacesViewBase) is the one real place all of that lives.

box-button.title: box-button
box-button.text: A button custom element used for navigating between sub-pages or opening dialogs, styled as a box row with an optional icon/description and a trailing nav arrow. <moz-box-button label="Settings" description="Manage your preferences"></moz-box-button> label Label for the button. Inherited from MozBoxBase (toolkit/content/widgets/lit-utils.mjs). description Descriptive text for the button. Inherited from MozBoxBase. iconSrc The src for an optional icon shown next to the label. Inherited from MozBoxBase. disabled Whether or not the button is disabled. accesskey Key used for keyboard access (property name accessKey, mapped to the accesskey attribute). parentDisabled Disabled by the parent's state (internal, see MozBoxBase/MozBaseInputElement plumbing). click --box-button-background-color Background color of the button row. --box-button-background-color-hover Background color on hover. --box-button-background-color-active Background color while pressed. --box-button-background-color-disabled Background color when disabled. --box-button-text-color Text color of the button row. --box-button-text-color-hover Text color on hover. --box-button-text-color-active Text color while pressed. --box-button-text-color-disabled Text color when disabled. Call the button's own click() method (it just forwards to buttonEl.click()) rather than dispatching synthetic events at the host, since that's the only interaction API MozBoxButton exposes. Don't assume the built-in arrow-right.svg chevron means the component navigates anywhere on its own, MozBoxButton renders it unconditionally to match its "navigating between sub-pages" JSDoc framing but has no href or default click handler, so you must wire up navigation yourself. moz-box.button.background.color.@base moz-box.button.background.color.active moz-box.button.background.color.disabled moz-box.button.background.color.hover moz-box.button.text.color.@base moz-box.button.text.color.active moz-box.button.text.color.disabled moz-box.button.text.color.hover

box-group.title: box-group
box-group.text: An element used to group combinations of moz-box-item, moz-box-link, and moz-box-button elements and provide the expected styles, including optional list/reorderable-list layout. <moz-box-group type="list"> <moz-box-item label="First"></moz-box-item> <moz-box-item label="Second"></moz-box-item> </moz-box-group> type The type of the group, either "list", "reorderable-list", or undefined. Note that "reorderable-list" only works with moz-box-item elements for now. (default) Slot for rendering various moz-box-* elements. static Slot for rendering non-reorderable moz-box-item elements. header Slot for header content, rendered above the list. footer Slot for footer content, rendered below the list. <index> Slots used to assign moz-box-* elements to <li> elements when the group is type="list". static-<index> Slots used to render moz-box-item elements that are not intended to be reorderable when the group is type="reorderable-list". reorder Fired when items are reordered via drag-and-drop or keyboard shortcuts. Detail contains draggedElement, targetElement, position, draggedIndex, targetIndex, and insertAt. scroll Re-dispatched on the host when a scroll container in the shadow tree scrolls, so light DOM listeners can observe scrolls that wouldn't otherwise cross the shadow boundary. getMozBoxElement Returns the moz-box element for a list item: either the item itself if it matches, or the first moz-box descendant (e.g. when the item is a setting-control wrapper). restoreTabindex Resets the tabindex on an item so it participates in focus traversal again. updateOptionRole Sets role="option" on the item's underlying moz-box element when the group renders as a reorderable list, and removes it otherwise. reorderArrayFromEvent Reorders an array based on the reorder event, for consumers that store items in an array. handleReorder Handles reordering of items in the list from a moz-reorderable-list event. Listen for "scroll" on the moz-box-group host itself, since #forwardScroll re-dispatches internal shadow-tree scroll events as a composed Event on the host specifically so listeners like a panel-list's hide-on-scroll can see them. Only use moz-box-item children when type="reorderable-list", the JSDoc and the itemselector ("moz-box-item:not([static])") passed to moz-reorderable-list both restrict dragging to that element, so moz-box-link/moz-box-button children won't become draggable. Don't manually set a slot attribute on children inside a type="list" or "reorderable-list" group, updated() overwrites item.slot to a numeric index (or `static-${i}`) for every list/static item on every re-render. moz-box.border.@base moz-box.border.color moz-box.border.radius.@base moz-box.border.radius.inner moz-box.border.width moz-box.icon.fill moz-box.icon.size moz-box.icon.stroke moz-box.padding

box-item.title: box-item
box-item.text: A custom element used for highlighting important information and/or providing context for specific settings, rendered as a box row with an optional icon, label, description, support link, and start/end action slots. <moz-box-item label="Setting name" description="Setting description"> <moz-button slot="actions" type="icon ghost" iconsrc="chrome://example.svg" aria-label="end action"></moz-button> </moz-box-item> label Label for the item. Inherited from MozBoxBase (toolkit/content/widgets/lit-utils.mjs). description Descriptive text for the item. Inherited from MozBoxBase. iconSrc The src for an optional icon shown next to the label. Inherited from MozBoxBase. supportPage The name of the SUMO support page to link to (attribute support-page). layout Layout style for the box content, reflected attribute. (default) Slot for the box item's content, which overrides label and description. support-link Slot for a custom support link element. description Slot for custom description content. actions Slot for the actions positioned at the end of the component container. actions-start Slot for the actions positioned at the start of the component container. support-link The optional "Learn more"-style support link, own render (not inherited from MozBoxBase, which has no shared parts). Use label/description/iconSrc or the default slot, never both, render() picks textTemplate() when label is set and falls back to <slot></slot> only when it's empty, so slotted custom content is silently dropped as soon as label has a value. Don't assume item.focus() focuses the item element itself, focus() only calls super.focus() when isFocusable (i.e. the item has a tabindex attribute, which moz-box-group sets in list-type groups); otherwise it delegates to the first or last slotted action element instead. moz-box.border.@base moz-box.border.color moz-box.border.radius.@base moz-box.border.radius.inner moz-box.border.width moz-box.icon.fill moz-box.icon.size moz-box.icon.stroke moz-box.padding

box-link.title: box-link
box-link.text: A link with a box-like shape that allows for custom title and description, rendering as an anchor with a trailing external-link nav icon. <moz-box-link label="Learn more" href="https://support.mozilla.org"></moz-box-link> label Label for the link. Inherited from MozBoxBase (toolkit/content/widgets/lit-utils.mjs). description Descriptive text for the link. Inherited from MozBoxBase. iconSrc The src for an optional icon. Inherited from MozBoxBase. href The href of the link. Ignored when supportPage is set (a support-link anchor is rendered instead). supportPage Name of a SUMO support page; when set, renders an is="moz-support-link" anchor instead of a plain href anchor (attribute support-page). --box-button-background-color Background color of the link row (shared with box-button, both render class="button"). --box-button-background-color-hover Background color on hover. --box-button-background-color-active Background color while pressed. --box-button-background-color-disabled Background color when disabled. --box-button-text-color Text color of the link row. --box-button-text-color-hover Text color on hover. --box-button-text-color-active Text color while pressed. --box-button-text-color-disabled Text color when disabled. Use supportPage for internal SUMO articles rather than passing that URL through href, render() branches on supportPage first and renders the is="moz-support-link" anchor exclusively, completely ignoring href when both are set. Don't expect the href-based link to stay in the current tab, the template hardcodes target="_blank" on that anchor with no property to override it, so it always opens a new tab/window. moz-box.button.background.color.@base moz-box.button.background.color.active moz-box.button.background.color.disabled moz-box.button.background.color.hover moz-box.button.text.color.@base moz-box.button.text.color.active moz-box.button.text.color.disabled moz-box.button.text.color.hover

breadcrumb.title: breadcrumb
breadcrumb.text: A breadcrumb navigation group. Renders its child moz-breadcrumb elements inside a <nav><ol> list, automatically assigning positional slots and marking the last breadcrumb as the current page via aria-current. Defined alongside a related moz-breadcrumb element (the individual breadcrumb link/label) in the same file. <moz-breadcrumb-group> <moz-breadcrumb label="Home" href="/"></moz-breadcrumb> <moz-breadcrumb label="Settings" href="/settings"></moz-breadcrumb> <moz-breadcrumb label="General"></moz-breadcrumb> </moz-breadcrumb-group> <index> Positional slots (0, 1, 2, ...) that each moz-breadcrumb child is automatically assigned to, one per <li> in the rendered <ol>. Let MozBreadcrumbGroup manage slot assignment and aria-current, update() calls setupBreadcrumbs() on every update, which always re-slots every moz-breadcrumb child by document order and stamps aria-current="page" onto the last one. Don't expect the final breadcrumb to stay a clickable link, once the group marks it aria-current="page", MozBreadcrumb's own render() drops the <a href> wrapper for any breadcrumb with ariaCurrent set and renders plain text instead. link.color.@base link.color.active link.color.hover link.color.visited link.focus.outline.offset moz-breadcrumb.gap moz-breadcrumb.icon.size moz-breadcrumb.link.color.@base moz-breadcrumb.link.color.active moz-breadcrumb.link.color.hover moz-breadcrumb.link.color.visited

button-group.title: button-group
button-group.text: A light layout wrapper around a group of buttons. **It promotes the primary button itself:** it watches its default slot for <button>/<moz-button> children and automatically moves whichever one is primary (class="primary", type="submit", the autofocus/default attribute, or moz-button type="primary"/"destructive") into the primary slot. **Then it reorders for the platform:** the primary button is moved to the platform-correct end of the group, start on Windows, end on macOS/Linux. <moz-button-group><button>Cancel</button><button class="primary">Save</button></moz-button-group> platform The detected platform ("linux" | "macosx" | "win"), set automatically from AppConstants.platform (falling back to navigator.platform sniffing). Not user-configurable. (default) Buttons in their natural order. On slotchange, any child recognized as a primary button is automatically moved to the primary slot. primary Explicit slot for a primary-styled button that lacks primary styling of its own, to control its position. Reordered to the platform-appropriate end of the group whenever platform changes. Set slot="primary" yourself on a primary button that does not carry primary styling, onSlotchange only auto-promotes a plain <button> with class="primary", type="submit", autofocus or default, or a <moz-button> whose type is primary or destructive. Assert on slot assignment rather than DOM or visual order in tests, #reorderLightDom() puts primary buttons first on Windows and last everywhere else and render() swaps the two slots to match. Don't set platform in markup, it is declared as { state: true } and assigned by #detectPlatform() in the constructor, so an attribute you write is ignored. Don't wrap the buttons in a container element, onSlotchange switches on child.localName and only ever promotes button and moz-button, so a wrapper leaves every child in the default slot unordered. Don't put class="primary" on a <moz-button> expecting promotion, that branch reads the type property instead, so only type="primary" or type="destructive" moves it. Don't rely on the light-DOM order you authored, #reorderLightDom() calls prepend or append on your own children, so the element rewrites its child order after every slotchange.

button.title: button
button.text: A button with multiple types and three sizes. <moz-button type="primary">Save</moz-button> label The button's label, will be overridden by slotted content. type The button type. The legal set is asserted by this contract, not read from source: Lit declares only `{ type: String }`, so the values live in moz-button.css's own selectors. `primary`, `destructive` and `split` are matched exactly; `ghost`, `icon`, `muted`, `menuitem` and `toolbar` are matched as words, which is what makes a compound like `icon ghost` work. `menuitem` and `toolbar` are context declarations set by the surrounding component rather than style choices. `default` has no rule of its own, it is the unstyled baseline set in the constructor. Two values Figma Code Connect still emits are not in this set. `neutral` and `icon neutral` match no CSS rule at all: the design system renamed that variant to `muted`, which is what both moz-button.css and Figma's own variables now say, and moz-button.figma.ts was never updated. `icon primary` matches only `[type~="icon"]`, because `[type="primary"]` is an exact match a compound cannot satisfy, so it renders as a plain icon button with no primary colour. size The button size. Options: `default`, `small`, `large`. disabled The disabled state. title The button's title attribute, used in shadow DOM and therefore not as an attribute on moz-button. tooltipText Set the title property; the title attribute will be used first. ariaLabel The button's aria-label attribute, used in shadow DOM and therefore not as an attribute on moz-button. ariaHasPopup The button's aria-haspopup attribute, indicates a popup element can be triggered by the button. ariaExpanded The button's aria-expanded attribute, indicates whether the controlled elements are displayed or hidden. ariaPressed The button's aria-pressed attribute, used in shadow DOM and therefore not as an attribute on moz-button. ariaChecked The button's aria-checked attribute, used in shadow DOM and therefore not as an attribute on moz-button. iconSrc Path to the icon that should be displayed in the button. attention Show a dot notification on the button if true. iconPosition The icon's position relative to the button label. Options: `start`, `end`. menuId A CSS selector string that identifies the associated panel-list menu element controlled by the button. parentDisabled When the parent of this component is disabled. accessKey Internal, maps the accesskey attribute to the accessKey JS property (mapped, not in the top JSDoc block but declared in static properties). hasVisibleLabel Internal, tracks whether or not the button has a visible label (state property, not a real attribute). (default) The button's content, overrides label property. click The click event. --button-outer-padding-inline Used to set the outer inline padding of toolbar style buttons. --button-outer-padding-block Used to set the outer block padding of toolbar style buttons. --button-outer-padding-inline-start Used to set the outer inline-start padding of toolbar style buttons. --button-outer-padding-inline-end Used to set the outer inline-end padding of toolbar style buttons. --button-outer-padding-block-start Used to set the outer block-start padding of toolbar style buttons. --button-outer-padding-block-end Used to set the outer block-end padding of toolbar style buttons. button The internal <button> element. chevron-button The dropdown-opening chevron on a split-type button. moz-button-label The button's internal label element. Use menuId pointing at a <panel-list> instead of writing custom open and close logic, the internal controller handles ARIA and open state for you. Use real slotted content instead of label when you need more than plain text. Don't set type="split" without also setting menuId, the chevron renders but has nothing to open. Don't expect a plain title HTML attribute to behave like a normal tooltip from outside, the component's own JSDoc notes it is used inside shadow DOM and mapped internally, not a typical reflected callout.title: callout
callout.text: FeatureCallout is a plain ES class (not a custom element) that renders ASRouter/onboarding tour messages as a popup anchored to a CSS-selected element. **Two anchoring modes:** a XUL <panel> in the browser chrome when a panel_position is configured, or an absolutely/relatively positioned <div> in content pages such as Firefox View. **It owns the tour, not just the popup:** it manages multi-screen tour progress via a pref, screen advancement, and focus/positioning lifecycle. const callout = new FeatureCallout({ win: window, pref: { name: "browser.example.feature-tour" }, location: "toolbar", context: "chrome", }); await callout.showFeatureCallout(); win Constructor option; the window the callout will render into. pref Constructor option; optional pref used to track progress through a multi-screen tour, e.g. { name: "browser.pdfjs.feature-tour" }. location Constructor option; string passed as the page when requesting messages from ASRouter and sending telemetry. context Constructor option; "chrome" when shown in the browser chrome, "content" when shown in a content page (e.g. Firefox View). browser Constructor option; the <browser> element the callout is being shown in/for. Defaults to win.docShell.chromeEventHandler. listener Constructor option; callback invoked on various callout lifecycle events to keep an external broker informed of state. theme Constructor option; see FeatureCallout's themePresets for accepted shapes. showFeatureCallout async showFeatureCallout(message?): requests (or accepts) a message from ASRouter and renders the callout for it; returns a Promise<boolean> for whether a message ended up shown. endTour endTour(skipFadeOut = false): tears down the current callout and its listeners, notifying the listener callback with 'end'. setupFeatureTourProgress Starts observing the configured pref (if any) to track/advance tour progress. teardownFeatureTourProgress Stops observing the pref and clears cached progress. featureTourProgress Getter returning the parsed current progress value read from the pref. onViewOpen Called by the urlbar controller listener; ends the tour when the urlbar view opens, to avoid overlapping popups. handleEvent Central DOM event handler for focus, keypress (Escape), visibilitychange, resize, popupshowing/popuphiding, and unload. getAutoFocusElement getAutoFocusElement({ selector, use_defaults }): resolves which element inside the callout should receive focus when it renders. Provide multiple anchors per screen when you can, _getAnchor() walks the anchors array and silently skips any whose selector doesn't resolve to a visible element, returning null (no callout rendered) only once every anchor has failed. Use panel_position only for context: "chrome" and arrow_position only for content pages, _createContainer() picks between a real XUL <panel> and an absolutely-positioned <div> based on which one is present, and needsPanel additionally requires MozXULElement to exist on the window. Don't call endTour() expecting the same FeatureCallout instance to be fully reusable afterward, it nulls this.pref via teardownFeatureTourProgress(), but setupFeatureTourProgress() (which registers the pref observer) only ever runs from the constructor, so tour-progress tracking never comes back on that instance. Don't assume a content (div-based) callout repositions itself when its scroll container scrolls, _addPositionListeners() only wires up window "resize" and popup "toggle" events to call _positionCallout(), not scroll on an ancestor.

card.title: card
card.text:
Cards contain content and actions about a single subject. The default type has no extra functionality; the "accordion" type initially hides its content behind a collapsed summary and can be expanded/collapsed by the user (or forced open via the expanded attribute).

Card content goes here.

 heading The heading text used for the card. headingLevel Specifies whether the heading renders as h1-h6 instead of a plain span (0 or unset renders a span). iconSrc Path to an optional icon shown next to the heading. type The card type. Default (unset) or "accordion". spacing The spacing level applied to the card. Default or "compact" (reduced spacing). expanded For accordion cards, whether the content section is expanded on initial render (and reflects current open/closed state after user toggling). role Optional ARIA role for the card's article element. summaryTabIndex Optional tabindex for the accordion summary element. cover-image Named slot for an optional cover image shown above the heading/content. (default) The card's content. Note: the class JSDoc labels this slot "content", but the rendered in both the default and accordion templates has no name attribute, so it is the unnamed/default slot, not a named "content" slot. toggle Fired (as a ToggleEvent with newState/oldState) when an accordion-type card's expanded state changes via user interaction with the
element. heading The card heading element. moz-card-heading-wrapper The heading's wrapping container. summary The element, only present when the card is expandable. Slot content as direct, unslotted children, despite the JSDoc's "@slot content" label, the actual template only renders an unnamed default slot (id="content-slot" for accordion cards, bare otherwise), so adding slot="content" to children keeps them from rendering at all. Don't pass a headingLevel outside 1-6 expecting an error, headingTextTemplate() falls back silently to a plain via `headingLevels[this.headingLevel] || headingLevels[0]`, so a typo like headingLevel="7" just loses heading semantics with no warning. card.background.color card.border.@base card.border.color card.border.radius.@base card.border.radius.compact card.border.width card.box.shadow.@base card.box.shadow.hover card.cover.image.border.radius card.cover.image.height.default card.cover.image.object.fit.default card.cover.image.object.position.default card.cover.image.padding.@base card.cover.image.padding.compact card.focus.outline card.font.size.@base card.font.size.compact card.gap.@base card.gap.article card.gap.compact card.header.background.color.@base card.header.background.color.active card.header.background.color.hover card.header.border.color.@base card.header.border.color.active card.header.border.color.hover card.header.text.color.@base card.header.text.color.active card.header.text.color.hover card.padding.@base card.padding.compact

checkbox.title: checkbox
checkbox.text: Modern Lit-based checkbox input with a label, description, and optional icon/support link. **A legacy XUL-style <checkbox> still exists** in the tree for older UI (toolkit/content/widgets/checkbox.js, registered as tag "checkbox"). It renders a checkbox-check image plus a checkbox-label-box (icon + label) and exposes only a simple reflected `checked` boolean, with attribute inheritance for disabled/checked/native/label/accesskey/src. **The attrs/slots/events below describe the modern one:** moz-checkbox, which is the actively-recommended implementation. <moz-checkbox label="Enable feature" checked></moz-checkbox> label The text of the label element. name The name of the checkbox input control. value The value of the checkbox input control. Defaults to "on" if unset. checked The state of the checkbox element; also controls whether the checkbox is initially rendered as checked. disabled The disabled state of the checkbox input. iconSrc The src for an optional icon. description Text for the description element that helps describe the checkbox. supportPage Name of the SUMO support page to link to. ariaLabel The aria-label text when there is no visible label. ariaDescription The aria-description text when there is no visible description. title The title attribute, mapped onto the inner input. change Redispatched when the checked state changes via user interaction. Put dependent controls in the slot="nested" slot instead of manually disabling them, MozBaseInputElement's updateNestedElements() sets their parentDisabled from `!this.checked || this.disabled` because moz-checkbox declares static activatedProperty = "checked", so nested elements go disabled whenever the box is unchecked, not only when the checkbox itself is disabled. Don't rely on form.reset() restoring a checked value you assigned with JS after the element connected, defaultChecked is captured exactly once in connectedCallback from the initial checked attribute/property, so later `.checked` assignments change the current value but not what formResetCallback() reverts to. Don't expect the classic <checkbox> element (toolkit/content/widgets/checkbox.js, which still ships alongside moz-checkbox) to have any interactive behavior, its checked getter/setter only toggles the checked attribute for CSS/image purposes, there's no click handler, keyboard toggling, or form participation built in. checkbox.margin.inline checkbox.size

chip.title: chip
chip.text: No generic 'chip' component exists in mozilla-central. The closest analog is ai-website-chip (browser/components/aiwindow/ui/components/ai-website-chip/ai-website-chip.mjs), but that is a distinct, single-purpose feature component (an AI-window website-reference chip), not a reusable generic chip primitive. Treat this as a dismissible chip-style UI, not a reusable Acorn primitive, the one real analog in mozilla-central (ai-website-chip) is purpose-built for a single feature, not a generic component to extend. Don't go looking for a generic chip class or shared styles to reuse, no such component exists yet, a new one needs its own real implementation rather than assuming one is hiding somewhere.

details.title: details
details.text: No dedicated Firefox component exists for a disclosure widget. Chrome UI that needs this behavior uses the native HTML <details>/<summary> elements directly rather than a wrapped Acorn component. Use the native <details>/<summary> elements directly for disclosure widgets, that's the real pattern chrome UI relies on today, not a wrapped Acorn component. Don't look for an acorn-details or similar wrapper before reaching for native <details>, no dedicated Firefox component exists for this behavior.

dialog.title: dialog
dialog.text:
MozDialog wraps the top-level element used by XUL/HTML dialog windows and in-content subdialogs: renders the button box (accept/cancel/extra1/extra2/disclosure) and a content slot, wires Enter/Escape handling, default-button focus and snapping, and window sizing/positioning helpers.

Body content

 subdialog Observed attribute, set on the document root; switches the dialog into subdialog-embedded styling by appending the in-content stylesheet. extra1-is-secondary Observed attribute; on non-Windows Unix platforms, moves the extra1 button to appear after the cancel button. buttons get/set property. Comma-delimited list of dlgtype values (accept, cancel, extra1, extra2, disclosure) to show; any dlgtype not listed is hidden. defaultButton get/set property, defaults to "accept". Which button's command fires when Enter is pressed; toggles the default attribute on that button. buttonlabel e.g. buttonlabelaccept, buttonlabelcancel, buttonlabelextra1, buttonlabelextra2, buttonlabeldisclosure. Per-button label override, read in _configureButtons(); falls back to dialog.properties localized defaults for accept/cancel/disclosure. buttonaccesskey e.g. buttonaccesskeyaccept, buttonaccesskeycancel. Per-button accesskey override, paired with the corresponding buttonlabel attribute. buttonid e.g. buttonidaccept, buttonidcancel. Per-button Fluent id override, used via document.l10n.setAttributes() when no explicit label is set. buttondisabledaccept Inherited to [dlgtype='accept']: disabled state of the accept button. buttonpack Inherited to .dialog-button-box as pack, for platform-specific button layout. buttonalign Inherited to .dialog-button-box as align. buttondir Inherited to .dialog-button-box as dir. buttonorient Inherited to .dialog-button-box as orient. (default) Dialog body content, rendered via an inside the shadow DOM's .box-inherit[part=content-box]. dialogaccept Cancelable Events-type event fired when the accept button (or Enter) is activated. dialogcancel Cancelable Events-type event fired when the cancel button (or Escape) is activated. dialogextra1 Cancelable Events-type event fired when the extra1 button is activated. dialogextra2 Cancelable Events-type event fired when the extra2 button is activated. dialogdisclosure Cancelable Events-type event fired when the disclosure button is activated. dialogclosing CustomEvent with detail { button }, fired immediately before window.close() on an uncanceled accept or cancel. acceptDialog Programmatically triggers the accept button's command. cancelDialog Programmatically triggers the cancel button's command. getButton getButton(dlgtype): returns the button element for the given dlgtype. buttonBox Getter returning the shadow DOM's .dialog-button-box element. moveToAlertPosition Positions the dialog window relative to its opener, alert-style. centerWindowOnScreen Centers the dialog window on the screen. fieldset.title: fieldset
fieldset.text: Fieldset wrapper used to lay out form inputs consistently, with an optional legend (label), description, icon, badge, and support link. <moz-fieldset label="Related settings" description="Optional supporting text"> <moz-checkbox label="Option one"></moz-checkbox> </moz-fieldset> label The label for the fieldset's legend. description The description text for the fieldset. supportPage Name of the SUMO support page to link to (attribute: support-page). When unset, a named "support-link" slot is rendered instead so callers can supply their own link. headingLevel Renders the legend as h1-h6 instead of plain legend text. Default is -1 (no heading). disabled Disables the fieldset and, via a MutationObserver-style pass over children, propagates a disabled/parentDisabled state to nested form controls that support it. iconSrc Src for an optional icon shown next to the legend. badge Includes a moz-badge of this type next to the legend. Options: `beta`, `new`. ariaLabel Accessible label, mapped from the aria-label attribute. ariaOrientation Mapped aria-orientation attribute for the fieldset. role Mapped role attribute for the inner fieldset element, applied only when set. (default) The form inputs laid out inside the fieldset. support-link Rendered only when supportPage is not set; lets callers supply a custom support link element in place of the built-in moz-support-link. label The <legend> element. support-link The optional "Learn more"-style support link. inputs The wrapper around the fieldset's slotted inputs. Set headingLevel to 1-6 if you want the legend rendered as a heading element, anything else (including the default -1) falls through to a plain legend since HEADING_LEVEL_TEMPLATES only has entries for 1 through 6. Don't toggle disabled off on the fieldset expecting individually-disabled children to stay disabled, #updateChildDisabledState() runs querySelectorAll("*") over every descendant exposing a disabled or parentDisabled property and unconditionally clears/sets disabled on all of them with no per-child state tracking.

findbar.title: findbar
findbar.text: The in-page find toolbar (Ctrl+F). A classic, template-string XUL widget with no JSDoc; builds its UI from anonymous-content markup addressed by anonid rather than shadow-DOM slots, and drives find state via a FindBar JSActor. <findbar browserid="content-browser" prefillwithselection="true"></findbar> browserid Read via getAttribute to resolve the associated <browser> the findbar operates on; set by embedding chrome. prefillwithselection Backs the prefillWithSelection JS property (getter returns getAttribute(...) != "false"); controls whether the find field is prefilled with the current selection. hidden Standard DOM property toggled by open()/close() to show or hide the bar. noanim Internal animation-suppression flag set during open()/close(), consumed by CSS. findbaropen Plain Event dispatched from open(). findbarclose Plain Event dispatched from close(). find Cancelable CustomEvent fired from _find() before executing a search; detail includes query, caseSensitive, matchDiacritics, entireWord, highlightAll, findPrevious. findagain Cancelable CustomEvent fired from onFindAgainCommand(). findhighlightallchange Cancelable CustomEvent fired from toggleHighlight(). findcasesensitivitychange Cancelable CustomEvent fired from _setCaseSensitivity(). finddiacriticmatchingchange Cancelable CustomEvent fired from _setDiacriticMatching(). findmatchescount Cancelable CustomEvent fired from _updateMatchesCount() with the current match count in detail. open close clear startFind onFindCommand onFindAgainCommand onFindSelectionCommand toggleHighlight toggleEntireWord updateControlState onFindResult onMatchesCountResult onHighlightFinished onCurrentSelection shouldFocusContent destroy getElement --findbar-border-top-width Top border width of the findbar. --findbar-container-height Height of the findbar's inner container. --findbar-padding-block Block padding of the findbar. --findbar-height Overall computed height of the findbar. Pass an explicit mode such as this.FIND_NORMAL when calling open(), called bare it only sets findMode "if (mode != undefined)" and otherwise silently keeps whatever mode was left over from the previous session. Don't expect setting the browserid attribute alone, or reading the browser getter, to register the finder, connectedCallback only wires up finder.addResultListener and setFindbarInActor as a side effect of actually assigning to the browser property. Don't call toggleHighlight(true) again expecting a re-highlight after page content changes, the method short-circuits with "if (highlight === this._highlightAll) return" before ever calling finder.highlight(), so toggling to the same value twice in a row does nothing.

five-star.title: five-star
five-star.text: Renders five stars (empty, half, or full) derived from a numeric rating rounded to the nearest half. When selectable is set, clicking a star updates the rating and dispatches a select event with the new rating in its detail. <moz-five-star rating="3.5" selectable></moz-five-star> rating The rating out of 5. Rounded to the nearest half to decide each star's fill state. selectable Whether the stars can be clicked to set a new rating. title Not rendered directly; when truthy (or when selectable is true) it suppresses the component's default localized "rating out of 5" label, on the assumption a real accessible name is supplied elsewhere. select CustomEvent dispatched (detail: { rating }) when a star is clicked and selectable is true. getStars Returns the current five-item array of { rating, fill } used to render each star ('full' | 'half' | 'empty'). getStarElementRating Reads the rating value off a given star element's rating attribute. onClick Click handler for an individual star; updates rating and dispatches select when selectable is true. Set selectable before listening for select, onClick returns early when it is false so the event never fires. Set title whenever you set selectable, render() suppresses the component's own data-l10n-id="moz-five-star-rating" as soon as either is truthy, leaving the role="img" wrapper with no accessible name if title is empty. Read the new value from the select event's detail.rating or from the reflected rating attribute, onClick assigns this.rating before dispatching. Don't listen for select on an ancestor, the CustomEvent is dispatched without bubbles or composed, so it only fires on the moz-five-star element itself. Don't expect a selectable widget to produce the half values it can display, getStars() rounds to the nearest half for rendering but onClick reads the star's rating attribute with parseInt, so a click always yields a whole number. Don't treat selectable as keyboard accessible, the stars are plain <span>s with a click handler and no tabindex or button role, so they can only be operated with a pointer.

icon-button.title: icon-button
icon-button.text: The icon-only usage mode of moz-button: an iconSrc is set with no visible label text, and type includes the "icon" token (optionally combined with "ghost") so the button renders as a square icon-only control. **Not a separate registered custom element.** It is documented separately here because it is a distinct, commonly-used configuration of moz-button; see the "button" component for the full element API. <moz-button type="icon ghost" iconsrc="chrome://global/skin/icons/edit-copy.svg" title="Copy"></moz-button> iconSrc Path to the icon displayed in the button. Required for icon-button usage: with no slotted/label text, this is the only visible content. type Must include the "icon" token to get icon-only sizing/layout (CSS selector `[type~="icon"]:not(.labelled)`). Supported combinations in moz-button.mjs/.css: "icon" (default theme) and "icon ghost" (ghost theme, via `[type~="ghost"]`). Figma Code Connect (moz-button.figma.ts) also lists "icon primary" and "icon neutral", but no matching CSS rule exists for those combos: `[type="primary"]` is an exact match, not a `~=` token match, so "icon primary" does not pick up primary styling. title Used as the accessible/tooltip label when there is no visible text label (common for icon-only buttons since title is rendered on the shadow-DOM button element). ariaLabel Accessible name for the button when there is no visible label text. size Options: `default`, `small`, `large`. Affects icon-button square dimensions via `--button-size-icon(-small|-large)`. disabled The disabled state. attention Shows a notification dot on the icon button (badged class applied when iconSrc or type includes "icon" and attention is true). menuId CSS selector identifying an associated panel-list menu; integrates the icon button with panel-list open/close and aria-expanded/aria-haspopup state. click The click event. Always set title or ariaLabel, there's no visible text label at all in this mode, so one of the two is the only accessible name a screen reader gets. Use type="icon ghost" for a lower-emphasis icon button, it's a supported combination in moz-button.mjs/.css. Don't use "icon primary" or "icon neutral", even though Figma Code Connect shows them as options: no matching CSS rule was found for either combo, [type="primary"] is an exact match not a ~= token match, so "icon primary" won't actually pick up primary styling. Don't leave menuId unset if you need a dropdown affordance, without it there's no real panel-list wiring for open/close state or aria-expanded/aria-haspopup. button.icon.fill button.icon.stroke button.padding.icon button.size.icon.@base button.size.icon.large button.size.icon.small

infobar.title: infobar
infobar.text: A dismissable, prioritized notification bar shown at the top of browser content (e.g. permission prompts, site warnings). **Two layers, classified differently:** a NotificationBox container manages it, and it is rendered as a <notification-message> element that extends the modern Lit-based moz-message-bar component. The notification-message layer itself is classic (no JSDoc), lazily registered the first time a notification is shown. <notification-message type="warning" dismissable="true" message="Firefox prevented this site from asking you to install software." supportPage="unwanted-software"></notification-message> value Notification id, set via setAttribute("value", type); used to look up a specific open notification. type Derived from priority: "system", "critical", "info", or "warning"; drives icon/color styling. Inherited property from moz-message-bar. message-bar-type Set unconditionally to "infobar" by appendNotification(); internal CSS-targeting hook, not caller-facing config. dismissable Inherited from moz-message-bar; controls whether the close button is shown. heading Inherited property from moz-message-bar for an optional bold heading line. message Inherited property from moz-message-bar; the notification's body text (also settable via the label setter, which accepts a string or an {l10n-id, l10n-args} object). supportPage Inherited from moz-message-bar; when set, renders a "Learn more" support link. priority Plain JS instance property (0-9, PRIORITY_SYSTEM through PRIORITY_CRITICAL_HIGH) set by appendNotification(); determines the type attribute. persistence Plain JS instance property; number of location changes the notification survives before auto-removal. timeout Plain JS instance property; a timestamp after which the notification is treated as expired. role Managed internally via setAlertRole(); typically "alert", not caller-set. message Inherited from moz-message-bar; falls back to the internal message span if empty. support-link Inherited from moz-message-bar; link-type buttons added via setButtons() are placed here. actions Light-DOM span (class notification-button-container) populated by setButtons() with command/primary buttons. AlertActive Plain Event dispatched right after a notification is shown, for accessibility APIs. message-bar:close Inherited from moz-message-bar; CustomEvent dispatched in disconnectedCallback(). message-bar:user-dismissed Inherited from moz-message-bar; cancelable CustomEvent dispatched from dismiss(); if not defaultPrevented, the bar closes and removes itself. appendNotification On the owning NotificationBox; creates and shows a notification-message. removeNotification removeCurrentNotification removeAllNotifications removeTransientNotifications getNotificationWithValue close setButtons dismiss --info-bar-background-color Infobar background color. --info-bar-background-color-configurable Per-notification override, settable via element.style on the instance. --info-bar-text-color Infobar text color. --info-bar-box-shadow Infobar box shadow. --info-bar-border-color Infobar border color. --info-bar-margin-block-start Top margin of the infobar. --info-bar-margin-inline Inline margin of the infobar. --info-bar-margin-block-end Bottom margin of the infobar. --message-bar-border-color Shared with moz-message-bar; border color. --message-bar-border-radius Shared with moz-message-bar; border radius. --message-bar-icon-container-margin-block-start Top margin of the icon container. --message-bar-icon-container-padding Padding of the icon container. Await appendNotification()'s returned promise before touching the notification further, it resolves only after the Lit-based moz-message-bar has flushed its update (and, for l10n labels, after document.l10n.translateFragment), so the shadow DOM and alert role aren't guaranteed to exist before that. Don't insert a notification-message element outside the stack a NotificationBox created, its close()/control getter walks up via this.closest(".notificationbox-stack")._notificationBox, a back-reference only set inside NotificationBox's own stack getter, so a manually-placed notification throws when closed. Don't give a button a popup id and expect a graceful no-op if it's wrong, setButtons calls document.getElementById(popup).openPopup(...) directly with no null check, so a missing popup id throws at click time. info-bar.border.color info-bar.margin toolbarseparator.color

input-color.title: input-color
input-color.text: A labeled color swatch input backed by a native <input type="color">, used to pick a CSS color value. <moz-input-color label="Background" value="#7293C9"></moz-input-color> value A CSS hex value shown in the swatch area. name Name associated with the nested native input element; useful in forms. label The text of the label shown next to the swatch. change Redispatched from the native input's change event when the user commits a new color value (this.value is updated first, then the change event is re-fired from the host so it crosses the shadow boundary). Treat this as a thin wrapper around the native color input rather than a full moz-input-* control, MozInputColor doesn't extend MozBaseInputElement and only declares value, name, and label, so disabled, description, and support-page from sibling inputs simply don't exist here. Don't pass a non-hex or invalid value expecting the component to validate or normalize it, MozInputColor binds .value straight to the native <input type="color"> with no validation of its own, so whatever the browser does with a bad value is all you get. moz-input-color.background.color.@base moz-input-color.background.color.active moz-input-color.background.color.hover moz-input-color.border.color.@base moz-input-color.border.color.active moz-input-color.border.color.hover moz-input-color.border.radius moz-input-color.gap moz-input-color.space.padding.block moz-input-color.space.padding.inline moz-input-color.swatch.border.color moz-input-color.swatch.border.radius moz-input-color.swatch.size moz-input-color.text.color.@base moz-input-color.text.color.active moz-input-color.text.color.hover

input-folder.title: input-folder
input-folder.text: A labeled, read-only text field paired with a moz-button that opens the native folder picker (nsIFilePicker). Resolves the chosen path to a real nsIFile via IOUtils and shows a folder icon (a real per-folder icon when the chrome Services module is available, otherwise a generic fallback) next to the value. <moz-input-folder name="download-dir" label="Download folder"></moz-input-folder> label The text of the label element. Not a settable property. disabled The disabled state of the component. Inherited from MozBaseInputElement via MozInputText. readonly The readonly state of the input control; forced back to true on every update (willUpdate always resets it), since the value is only ever set via the folder picker, not typed directly. required The required state of the input control. Inherited from MozInputText. iconSrc The src for an optional icon in the label. Inherited from MozBaseInputElement via MozInputText. description Text for the description element that helps describe the input control. Inherited from MozBaseInputElement via MozInputText. supportPage Name of the SUMO support page to link to (attribute: support-page). Inherited from MozBaseInputElement via MozInputText. placeholder Text to display when the input has no value. Inherited from MozInputText. title The title attribute, mapped onto the inner input. Inherited from MozBaseInputElement via MozInputText. description Inherited from MozBaseInputElement: rendered when the description property is unset, letting callers supply richer description markup. support-link Inherited from MozBaseInputElement: rendered when supportPage is unset, letting callers supply a custom support link element. actions Own slot alongside the choose-folder button, for additional actions. input Native Event (bubbles) dispatched by openFolderPicker() after a folder is chosen, since the field itself is readonly and not directly typed into. change Native Event (bubbles) dispatched by openFolderPicker() after a folder is chosen. moz-input-folder-picker-close Test-only CustomEvent dispatched (only when Cu.isInAutomation) when the picker dialog closes without a value change, so tests can wait for the dialog to finish closing. hasServices Safely reports whether the privileged Services module is available in this context. getFolderFromPath Resolves a filesystem path string to a real nsIFile/IOUtils directory object. getInputIconSrc Computes the moz-icon:// URL for a given folder, or a generic folder icon fallback. openFolderPicker Opens the native folder picker (nsIFilePicker) and, if a new folder is chosen, updates value/folder and dispatches input/change. label The internal <label is="moz-label">, inherited from MozBaseInputElement's shared render(). support-link The optional support link, inherited from MozBaseInputElement's shared render(). Read folder in a change or input listener after a user picks, not after assigning value yourself, openFolderPicker sets the private folder before it assigns value and dispatches, whereas a programmatic value assignment resolves the folder asynchronously in willUpdate. Set dialogTitle, it is passed straight to nsIFilePicker.init as the dialog's title and the constructor defaults it to an empty string. Don't set readonly to false, willUpdate forces it back to true on every change to that property, so the inner input can never be made editable. Don't treat displayValue as the value, inputTemplate renders displayValue || value but value stays the real folder path that the folder getter and form submission use. Don't expect input or change when the user cancels the picker or re-picks the folder already selected, openFolderPicker returns early on both. Don't assume a non-empty value means a real directory, getFolderFromPath catches an invalid path and returns null, leaving folder null while value keeps the bad string.

MozInputSearch:search Bubbling, composed CustomEvent (detail: { query: value }) dispatched 500ms after the user stops typing, or immediately/synchronously by clear() if the field had a value. clear Clears the value (on both the property and the underlying input element) and synchronously dispatches MozInputSearch:search if the field had a value. label The internal <label is="moz-label">, inherited from MozBaseInputElement's shared render(). support-link The optional support link, inherited from MozBaseInputElement's shared render(). Don't set readonly on a search input, its inputTemplate overrides the base and never passes readonly to the inner input, so the property reflects onto the host and changes nothing. Don't rely on input or change to observe clear(), it only dispatches MozInputSearch:search, and only when the value was non-empty to begin with. Don't remove the element within 500ms of the last keystroke and expect the final search, disconnectedCallback clears the pending debounce timer.

label.title: label
label.text: A customized built-in <label is="moz-label">. Its class extends StylesMixin(HTMLLabelElement, styles), so it is a subclass of HTMLLabelElement that also adopts moz-label.css onto its root. **Accesskey rendering:** it underlines, or appends in parentheses, the character in its text content matching its accesskey, following the platform convention of whether accesskeys are shown underlined at all. **Click forwarding:** it focuses and activates the control referenced by its control attribute, or the labelable control it wraps, when clicked. <label is="moz-label" accesskey="s" control="save-button">Save</label> accesskey Key used for keyboard access; also propagated onto the labeled control element. Only the first character is used. shownaccesskey A key to underline for display purposes without registering it as the real accesskey; works around multiple-accesskey elements being focused instead of activated. enable-center-crop Presence-only. Sets crop="center" and, if no value attribute is set yet, copies the element's current textContent into it. While present, the overridden textContent getter returns the value attribute instead of the element's real text. control The id of the control this label is for; used to look up labeledControlElement. formatAccessKey Re-renders the underlined/parenthesized accesskey markup inside the label's text content; runs automatically on connect and whenever the label's content or accesskey attribute changes. Set the accessKey property rather than the accesskey attribute when the key should also register on the control, only the property setter forwards it via control.setAttribute("accesskey", val). Use shownaccesskey instead of accesskey when the control already registers its own, it underlines the character for display without adding a second real accesskey to the element. Don't point control at an element inside the same shadow root, labeledControlElement resolves it with document.getElementById, so it comes back null and the click handler silently does nothing. Don't expect clicking the label to toggle an HTML checkbox referenced by control, _onClick only focuses it and special-cases XUL checkbox/radio localNames, so use the native for attribute if you want real label activation. Don't rely on the accesskey underline being visible everywhere, formatAccessKey returns early unless the platform underline check passes, which is off on macOS. Don't read textContent after setting enable-center-crop, the getter is overridden to return the value attribute instead of the element's real text.

message-bar.title: message-bar
message-bar.text: A message bar element used to display important information to users, with an icon derived from its type, optional heading, dismiss button, actions, and support link. <moz-message-bar type="warning" heading="Heads up" message="Something needs your attention." dismissable></moz-message-bar> type The type of the displayed message, drives the icon shown. Values with dedicated icon/l10n mappings in code: info, warning, success, error, critical (critical uses the same icon/l10n as error and is a legacy alias; Storybook's documented options list only info/warning/success/error, while the Figma Code Connect file also references "critical" and "information" as design-side type names). heading The heading of the message. message The message text. dismissable Whether the message bar shows a close/dismiss button. supportPage SUMO support page stub; when set, renders a built-in support link after the message. messageL10nId Fluent l10n ID for the message. messageL10nArgs JSON-stringified args for the message l10n ID. role ARIA role for the message bar, reflected as an attribute. Defaults to "alert". message Overrides the message/messageL10nId text content with custom markup (e.g. a message containing an inline link). actions Action buttons (e.g. moz-button elements) shown at the end of the message bar. support-link Rendered when supportPage is unset, letting callers supply a custom support link. message-bar:close Fired when the message bar is removed from the DOM (disconnectedCallback), regardless of cause. message-bar:user-dismissed Fired when the user clicks the dismiss/close button, before the element removes itself; cancelable: calling preventDefault() stops the automatic close(). support-link The optional "Learn more"-style support link. Rely on dismiss()'s cancelable "message-bar:user-dismissed" event instead of wiring your own close-button handler, close() (and the resulting removal) only runs when that event isn't preventDefault()-ed. Use the default role="alert" only for messages that truly need to interrupt, it reflects as an attribute so you can see exactly what's driving the announcement behavior. Don't set supportPage together with slotted support-link content expecting them to combine, supportLinkTemplate() renders the generated moz-support-link anchor or the slot, never both, so supportPage silently drops your slotted content. Don't treat "message-bar:close" (fired from disconnectedCallback) as proof the user dismissed the bar, it fires on any removal from the DOM, not just a close-button click. moz-message-bar.actions.button.padding moz-message-bar.actions.gap moz-message-bar.background.color.@base moz-message-bar.background.color.critical moz-message-bar.background.color.success moz-message-bar.background.color.warning moz-message-bar.border.color moz-message-bar.border.radius moz-message-bar.border.width moz-message-bar.close.margin.block-start moz-message-bar.close.margin.inline-end moz-message-bar.container.gap moz-message-bar.container.min-height moz-message-bar.container.padding.block moz-message-bar.container.padding.inline moz-message-bar.content.gap moz-message-bar.content.padding.block moz-message-bar.content.padding.inline moz-message-bar.icon.background.color.@base moz-message-bar.icon.background.color.critical moz-message-bar.icon.background.color.success moz-message-bar.icon.background.color.warning moz-message-bar.icon.color moz-message-bar.icon.container.align-items moz-message-bar.icon.container.border.@base moz-message-bar.icon.container.border.color moz-message-bar.icon.container.border.radius moz-message-bar.icon.container.border.radius-end-end moz-message-bar.icon.container.border.radius-end-start moz-message-bar.icon.container.border.radius-start-end moz-message-bar.icon.container.border.radius-start-start moz-message-bar.icon.container.height moz-message-bar.icon.container.margin.block.start.@base moz-message-bar.icon.container.margin.block.start.offset moz-message-bar.icon.container.padding-block-start moz-message-bar.icon.container.padding.@base moz-message-bar.icon.container.padding.offset moz-message-bar.icon.size moz-message-bar.message.margin.inline-end moz-message-bar.text.color moz-message-bar.text.container.gap moz-message-bar.text.container.padding.block moz-message-bar.text.content.gap

page-header.title: page-header
page-header.text: A header component for providing context about a specific page: a heading, optional icon, badge, description, support link, back button, and breadcrumbs. <moz-page-header heading="Settings" description="Manage your preferences" backbutton></moz-page-header> heading The page title text. description Secondary text shown under the heading. iconSrc Src for an optional icon shown next to the heading. supportPage Optional SUMO support page slug (attribute: support-page) for a related support article link. backButton Whether the header includes a back button; fires navigate-back when clicked. badge Includes a moz-badge of this type with matching text. Options: `beta`, `new`. headingLevel Heading level to render (1-6). Defaults to 2. breadcrumbs Container for a moz-breadcrumb-group, shown above the heading. navigate-back Fired when the back button is clicked, indicating backwards navigation should occur. support-link The optional "Learn more"-style support link. Attach any "navigate-back" listener directly on the moz-page-header element, handleBack() dispatches a plain non-bubbling Event, so a delegated listener higher up the tree will never catch it. Don't pass a headingLevel outside 1-6, headingTemplate()'s switch silently falls back to rendering an <h2> for anything unrecognized instead of warning. Don't be surprised when adding or removing description moves the support link, supportLinkTemplate() renders next to the heading only when there's no description, and after the description text otherwise.

page-nav-item.title: page-nav-item
page-nav-item.text: A navigation button intended to change the selected view within a moz-page-nav. **Renders two ways:** as a tab-role button by default, or as a link (external href or SUMO support-page) when href/supportPage is set. **Shares a file with its parent:** defined as a second customElements.define in the same file as moz-page-nav (class MozPageNavButton), documented here as its own component. <moz-page-nav-button view="general" iconsrc="chrome://global/skin/icons/settings.svg">General</moz-page-nav-button> href Optional URL for an external link if not a support page URL; when set, the button renders as an <a target="_blank"> instead of a <button>. iconSrc The chrome:// URL for the icon used for the button (reflected attribute). selected Whether the button is currently selected; managed by the parent moz-page-nav based on currentView, but reflects the button's own state. supportPage Optional short name for a support page a secondary link should launch to (attribute: support-page); when set, renders as a moz-support-link anchor. title Title used for the button or link; should always be set so the control is still identifiable when moz-page-nav is collapsed and its slotted text is hidden. Used in shadow DOM, not reflected as an attribute on the host. view Read via getAttribute("view") (not a declared Lit property): identifies which view this button activates; compared against the parent moz-page-nav's currentView. (default) Used to append the button's (typically l10n) label text. change-view Fired (bubbles, composed) when the button is activated, so the parent moz-page-nav can update currentView/selection. activate Dispatches the change-view event and focuses the underlying button/link element. Accepts an options object with an optional focusVisible flag; called by moz-page-nav for keyboard arrow navigation between buttons. Always set title even though it isn't shown by default, moz-page-nav can collapse and hide the slotted label text, and title is what keeps the button identifiable once that happens. Set view to a value that really matches one of the parent moz-page-nav's view ids, activate() compares it directly against the parent's currentView. Don't try to control selected from outside to force a switch, it's managed by the parent moz-page-nav based on currentView, not a real standalone toggle. Don't set both href and supportPage expecting one to layer on the other, href only takes effect when supportPage isn't set.

page-nav-separator.title: page-nav-separator
page-nav-separator.text: It's just a plain <hr> with no dedicated class/tagName, not a distinct sub-component. **Correction to the 'no separator implementation' citation:** moz-page-nav.mjs does render a real separator, `${when(this.hasSecondaryNav, () => html`<hr />`)}`, placed between the primary-nav-group and secondary-nav-group in its own render() output. Rely on moz-page-nav.mjs's own hasSecondaryNav check to get the separator, it renders a real <hr> between the primary-nav-group and secondary-nav-group automatically once a secondary nav exists. Don't author this <hr> yourself or give it a class, moz-page-nav.mjs places it directly in its own render() output with no dedicated sub-component.

page-nav.title: page-nav
page-nav.text: A grouping of navigation buttons displayed at the page level, used to change the selected view, provide a heading, and link to external resources. Manages selection state across its slotted moz-page-nav-button children and supports a secondary/footer nav group. <moz-page-nav heading="Settings"> <moz-page-nav-button view="general">General</moz-page-nav-button> <moz-page-nav-button view="privacy">Privacy</moz-page-nav-button> </moz-page-nav> currentView The currently selected view; matched against each moz-page-nav-button's view attribute. heading A heading displayed at the top of the navigation. type The type of the component. "mobile" shows a hamburger menu button before the logo/heading; default (unset) shows the standard nav. allowNoSelection When false (default), the component auto-selects the first visible button whenever currentView does not match any button. When true, a non-matching currentView is allowed to persist without forcing a selection (used by about:preferences for sub-pages/search-results states where no category should be highlighted). pageNavButtons Internal/read state: the array of all slotted primary moz-page-nav-button elements, derived from slotchange. secondaryNavButtons Internal/read state: the array of all slotted secondary-nav moz-page-nav-button elements, derived from slotchange. (default) Used to append moz-page-nav-button elements to the primary navigation. subheading Used to append page-specific search input or notification content below the heading. secondary-nav Used to append a secondary/footer group of moz-page-nav-button elements, separated from the primary group by an <hr> when present. Found in render()/onSecondaryNavChange but not documented in the class JSDoc. Hide a moz-page-nav-button with CSS (opacity: 0, visibility: hidden, display: none) or the hidden property, checkElementVisibility() checks all of these before treating a button as selectable. Rely on updateNavButtonsState() running in updated() to auto-select the first visible button when currentView matches nothing, you don't need a fallback-selection effect of your own. Don't assume allowNoSelection=true alone prevents auto-selection, updateNavButtonsState() only skips forcing a selection when currentView already holds a non-matching value; leaving currentView empty still auto-selects the first visible button. Don't set both href and support-page on a moz-page-nav-button expecting href to still work, linkTemplate() checks supportPage first, so support-page silently wins and href is ignored. Don't mix moz-page-nav-buttons with iconSrc and without it in the same nav, the component's own docs note this isn't supported and will look inconsistent. moz-page-nav.border.color moz-page-nav.button.background.color.@base moz-page-nav.button.background.color.active moz-page-nav.button.background.color.hover moz-page-nav.button.background.color.selected moz-page-nav.button.border.color.@base moz-page-nav.button.border.color.active moz-page-nav.button.border.color.hover moz-page-nav.button.border.radius.@base moz-page-nav.button.border.radius.focused moz-page-nav.button.gap moz-page-nav.button.indicator.background.color moz-page-nav.button.indicator.width moz-page-nav.button.padding.@base moz-page-nav.button.padding.small moz-page-nav.button.text.color.@base moz-page-nav.button.text.color.active moz-page-nav.button.text.color.hover moz-page-nav.button.text.color.selected moz-page-nav.focus.outline.offset moz-page-nav.focus.padding moz-page-nav.gap moz-page-nav.heading.logo.size moz-page-nav.hr.background.color moz-page-nav.margin.block.start moz-page-nav.margin.inline.start page.main.content.width page.space.block.start

panel-item.title: panel-item
panel-item.text: A single actionable row inside a panel-list menu (button, checkbox item, or submenu trigger). A plain modern custom element (no JSDoc) with its own shadow root; coordinates with its owning panel-list for keyboard navigation and accesskey lifecycle. <panel-list> <panel-item accesskey="N">New</panel-item> <panel-item type="checkbox" checked>Toggle Setting</panel-item> <panel-item badge-type="new">Save</panel-item> <panel-item submenu="example-sub-menu"> Has a submenu <panel-list slot="submenu" id="example-sub-menu"> <panel-item>Submenu Item One</panel-item> </panel-list> </panel-item> </panel-list> accesskey Observed attribute; mirrored to the internal label's accessKey. Stashed and blanked while the owning panel is closed, restored on the panel's shown event (workaround for bug 1588156). type Observed attribute, getter/setter, defaults to "button". Only recognized special value is "checkbox", which sets role=menuitemcheckbox and enables the checked property. disabled Observed attribute, getter/setter; reflected onto the internal button. badge-type Observed attribute; lazily creates a <moz-badge> element after the label and sets its type, or removes it when cleared. aria-haspopup Observed attribute; mirrored onto the internal button as an ARIA passthrough. submenu Not observed (read only once at connectedCallback via the hasSubmenu getter). Identifies the id of a nested panel-list placed in the submenu slot. badged Pure CSS attribute-selector hook (:host([badged]) button::after draws a small dot); not read by any JS in this component. Distinct from badge-type. checked Getter/setter, only meaningful when type="checkbox"; otherwise the getter always returns false and the setter is a no-op. (default) Hidden default slot; its assigned text content is harvested via MutationObserver into the internal label, since a real <slot> can't be used directly for the label. support-link Named slot for an inline link element. submenu Named slot for a nested panel-list; its assigned node is moved directly into the shadow root when hasSubmenu is true. click focus setArrowKeyRTL setSubmenuContents --panel-item-badge-inset-block-start Position of the CSS-only badge dot. --panel-item-badge-inset-inline-start Position of the CSS-only badge dot. --panel-item-badge-size Size of the CSS-only badge dot. --panel-item-badge-background-color Background color of the CSS-only badge dot, set inline to var(--color-accent-primary). --panel-item-button-border-radius Border radius of the internal button. --panel-item-button-margin Margin of the internal button. --panel-item-button-padding Padding of the internal button. --panel-item-button-padding-inline-start Inline-start padding of the internal button. --panel-item-button-padding-inline-start-offset Added on top of --panel-item-button-padding-inline-start; lets a subclass/consumer nudge the icon-accommodating inline-start padding without overriding the whole value. button The internal <button> element. label The internal label element showing the item's text. Use badge-type instead of manually inserting a <moz-badge>, it lazily creates and removes the badge element for you. Set accesskey normally even inside a panel that opens and closes often, it's stashed and restored automatically across the owning panel's open/close cycle (a real workaround for bug 1588156). Don't rely on badged alone to show a notification dot with real content, it's a pure CSS attribute-selector hook with no JS behavior at all, distinct from badge-type which actually creates the badge element. Don't set submenu after the item has already connected, it's only read once in connectedCallback, not an observed attribute. panel-item.badge.inset.block.start panel-item.badge.inset.inline.start panel-item.button.border.radius panel-item.button.margin panel-item.button.padding.@base panel-item.button.padding.inline.start.@base panel-item.button.padding.inline.start.offset panel-item.fill panel-menuitem.border.radius panel-menuitem.margin.@base panel-menuitem.margin.inline panel-menuitem.padding.@base panel-menuitem.padding.block panel-menuitem.padding.inline

panel-list-item.title: panel-list-item
panel-list-item.text: There is no upstream distinction between this entry and Panel Item. **Same class, same registration:** both ids refer to the exact same class (PanelItem) and the exact same customElements.define("panel-item", PanelItem) registration, in the same file as panel-list. The Acorn API's coverage table lists them separately, but there is no separate implementation for panel-list-item; this entry documents the same underlying class as the panel-item id. **Corrected kind:** PanelItem extends plain HTMLElement (no XUL/MozElementMixin base), so it is modern, matching the panel-item id's own classification of the identical class. <panel-list> <panel-item accesskey="s">Settings</panel-item> <panel-item type="checkbox" checked>Show toolbar</panel-item> </panel-list> type Observed attribute. "checkbox" gives the internal button role="menuitemcheckbox" and an aria-checked reflection; any other value (default "button") gives role="menuitem". disabled Observed attribute; get/set property. Toggles the disabled attribute on the internal button. checked get/set property (not in observedAttributes). Only meaningful when type="checkbox"; toggles the checked attribute and the internal button's aria-checked. accesskey Observed attribute. Moved onto an internal XUL <label> for display; temporarily cleared while the parent panel-list is closed and restored when it reopens (bug 1588156 workaround). badge-type Observed attribute. When set, inserts a <moz-badge type="..."> element right after the label; removed when the attribute is cleared. submenu Presence flag (hasAttribute("submenu")), read once in connectedCallback. When present, adds a submenu-icon and a named "submenu" slot for a nested panel-list, and sets has-submenu on the parent panel-list. aria-haspopup Observed attribute; forwarded verbatim to the internal button's aria-haspopup. (default) Text content; read via a MutationObserver and copied into the internal <label> element (the assigned nodes themselves stay hidden). support-link Named slot rendered alongside the button, e.g. for a 'Learn more' link next to the item. submenu Named slot, only created when the submenu attribute is present; holds a nested panel-list acting as this item's submenu. click Synthesizes a click on the internal button. focus Focuses the internal button. --panel-item-badge-inset-block-start Block-start inset of the badge relative to the item. --panel-item-badge-inset-inline-start Inline-start inset of the badge relative to the item. --panel-item-badge-size Size of the CSS-only badge dot, set inline on :host([badged]) button::after. --panel-item-badge-background-color Background color of the CSS-only badge dot, set inline to var(--color-accent-primary). --panel-item-button-border-radius Corner radius of the internal button. --panel-item-button-margin Margin of the internal button. --panel-item-button-padding Padding of the internal button. --panel-item-button-padding-inline-start Inline-start padding of the internal button (accommodates a leading icon). --panel-item-button-padding-inline-start-offset Added on top of --panel-item-button-padding-inline-start; lets a subclass/consumer nudge the icon-accommodating inline-start padding without overriding the whole value. button The internal <button> element. label The internal label element showing the item's text. Follow panel-item's own guidance here too, this is the exact same class (PanelItem) and the exact same customElements.define("panel-item", PanelItem) registration, not a separate implementation. Use badge-type instead of manually inserting a <moz-badge>, same as panel-item, it lazily creates and removes the element for you. Don't go looking for a separate source file or distinct behavior under this name, panel-list.mjs is the only real source for both this id and panel-item. Don't set submenu after the item has already connected, it's a presence flag read once in connectedCallback, not an observed attribute.

panel-list.title: panel-list
panel-list.text: A menu/list container custom element that renders panel-item children, either as a native popover or, when embedded in a XUL <panel>, deferring positioning and open/close to that panel. **No JSDoc:** class PanelList is defined in the same file as PanelItem (panel-item). **Corrected kind:** PanelList extends plain HTMLElement (no XUL/MozElementMixin base), the same non-XUL heritage as panel-item, which this inventory already classifies as modern. <panel-list> <panel-item>Item one</panel-item> <panel-item>Item two</panel-item> </panel-list> open Reflected get/set property; observed attribute. Toggling it drives attributeChangedCallback, which calls onShow()/onHide() (alignment, popover show/hide, focus, hide-listener registration). stay-open get/set stayOpen. When present (and the anchor doesn't have a submenu), addHideListeners() is skipped entirely, so the panel never auto-dismisses; intended for inspecting panels/submenus in Storybook. suppress-contextmenu When present, addHideListeners() also registers a contextmenu listener so context menus are suppressed inside the open panel. Never wired up when stay-open short-circuits addHideListeners(). min-width-from-anchor When present, setAlign() uses the anchor element's width (instead of the panel's own measured width) as the effective width for alignment, and sets min-width to the anchor's width. popover Managed internally by initializePopover()/show(): set to "auto" (light-dismissable) or "manual", or removed entirely when embedded in a XUL panel or acting as a submenu. Not meant to be set directly by consumers. has-submenu Set on the panel-list by a child panel-item when that item has a submenu, so submenu-specific layout CSS can apply. Internal state, not consumer-set. align Internal, computed by setAlign(): "left" or "right", recorded so CSS can position the panel relative to its anchor. valign Internal, computed by setAlign(): "top" or "bottom". inxulpanel Internal; reflects whether this panel-list is embedded inside a XUL <panel> (parentIsXULPanel()), which changes how positioning and open/close are handled. showing Internal, transient; set during layout measurement in setAlign()/setSubmenuAlign() to hide the panel until its position is computed, then removed. (default) panel-item elements (and other content) rendered as the menu's items, inside the shadow DOM's .list container. showing Dispatched (bubbles, composed) at the start of onShow(), before alignment is computed or the popover is shown. shown Dispatched after the panel is visible, alignment/focus are settled, and (if opened via keyboard) the first item is focused. hidden Dispatched from onHide(), after the popover is hidden (or immediately if popover isn't supported). show show(triggeringEvent, target): opens the panel, computing alignment relative to the anchor/target and using the native popover API when supported (or a XUL panel's openPopup when embedded). hide hide(triggeringEvent, { force }, eventTarget): closes the panel; force bypasses the ui.popup.disable_autohide pref. toggle toggle(triggeringEvent, target): calls show() or hide() depending on current open state. --panel-list-background-color Background color of the panel list. --panel-list-border-color Border color of the panel list. --panel-list-border-radius Corner radius of the panel list. --panel-list-box-shadow Drop shadow of the panel list. --panel-list-text-color Default text color for items in the list.
