Open a panel-list via show()/toggle() rather than setting the open attribute directly when correct positioning matters, show() is what populates lastAnchorNode and triggeringEvent that setAlign() uses, a bare open = true still renders but falls back to positioning against the host element itself. Don't expect a panel-item with type="checkbox" to toggle its own checked state on click, #setButtonAttributes only reflects whatever .checked already is, there's no built-in click handler that flips it. Don't rely on stay-open for shipping UI, addHideListeners() skips all click-outside/Escape/focus-loss/scroll/resize dismiss handling when it's set, and the inline comment notes it's intended only for Storybook inspection. panel-list.background.color.@base panel-list.border.color panel-list.border.radius panel-list.box.shadow.@base panel-list.text.color popup.background.color popup.border.color popup.border.radius popup.box.shadow

panel-manager.title: panel-manager
panel-manager.text: PanelMultiView and PanelView are plain ES classes (not custom elements) that attach behavior to <panelmultiview> and <panelview> XUL elements via a WeakMap-backed lazy association (AssociatedToNode.forNode). **PanelMultiView** manages a XUL <panel>'s open/close lifecycle and slide transitions between a main view and stacked subviews. **PanelView** wraps a single <panelview> and its header/sizing state. <panelmultiview mainViewId="appMenu-mainView" viewCacheId="appMenu-viewCache"> <panelview id="appMenu-mainView">...</panelview> </panelmultiview> mainViewId Attribute on <panelmultiview>; id of the <panelview> shown as the main view when the panel opens. viewCacheId Attribute on <panelmultiview>; id of an element that subviews are moved into (via _moveOutKids()) before the panel is removed, so they survive removePopup(). disablekeynav Attribute on <panelmultiview>; when present, arrow-key/Tab view navigation (the capturing keydown listener added on popupshowing) is not registered. lockpanelvertical Attribute read from the first open view's node (openViews[0].node); when "true", a subview's height is locked to the previous view's height instead of resizing to fit. mainview Set on a <panelview>'s node by the mainview setter, true while that view is being shown as the panel's main view (vs. a pushed subview). no-back-button Attribute on a <panelview>; suppresses the automatic back button that headerText would otherwise prepend. has-custom-header Attribute on a <panelview>; keeps a custom header element from being removed when headerText is cleared. mainview-with-header Attribute on a <panelview>; same effect as has-custom-header, keeps the header even with no title. ViewShowing Dispatched (async, cancelable via addBlocker on the detail) on a <panelview> when it is about to be opened as the main view or a subview; handlers can populate the view or cancel showing it. ViewShown Dispatched on a <panelview> once it becomes the active, visible view. ViewHiding Dispatched on a <panelview> when it is closed (navigated away from or the panel is closing). PanelMultiViewHidden Dispatched on the <panelmultiview> node after the underlying panel's popuphidden handling and view teardown complete. PanelMultiView.openPopup static(panelNode, ...args): opens the <panel> containing a <panelmultiview>, showing its mainViewId view; if the panel has no <panelmultiview>, opens the panel directly. PanelMultiView.hidePopup static(panelNode, animate): closes the <panel>, or the <panelmultiview> instance's hidePopup if present. PanelMultiView.removePopup static(panelNode): moves any child subviews to the view cache (if configured) and removes the panel from the document. PanelMultiView.getViewNode static(doc, id): returns the DOM node for a view id, falling back to the appMenu-viewCache template content. connect Instance: builds the viewcontainer/viewstack elements and wires popupshowing/popupshown/popuphidden listeners. disconnect Instance: removes event listeners set up by connect(). openPopup Instance: openPopup(anchor, options, ...args), async; shows the main view then calls the panel's native openPopup. hidePopup Instance: hidePopup(animate); closes the panel and synchronously closes all open views. showSubView Instance: showSubView(viewIdOrNode, anchor); slides in a subview. goBack Instance: navigates back to the previous view in the stack. closeAllViews Instance: raises ViewHiding for every open view, in reverse order. PanelView.isOpenIn Instance (PanelView): isOpenIn(panelMultiView); whether this view is the one currently open in the given PanelMultiView. PanelView.headerText Instance (PanelView) setter; adds, updates, or removes the view's .panel-header (with back button and separator) based on the given title. Set disablekeynav deliberately and only when you intend to lose all built-in keyboard navigation, it's checked once in the popupshowing handler, and when set, the keydown/mousemove listeners that drive arrow-key/Tab/Home/End navigation are never attached for that panel's entire lifetime, with no fallback. Don't call showSubView or goBack before the panel has ever been opened, openViews is only initialized inside connect(), so calling either beforehand throws a raw TypeError instead of the intended "Cannot show a subview in a closed panel" console error. Don't assume a second showSubView/goBack call fired mid-transition queues up, both check "if (!prevPanelView.active) return" with no error or logging, so a call arriving while a transition is already in flight is just silently dropped.

panel-separator.title: panel-separator
panel-separator.text: A plain <hr>, author-supplied light-DOM content placed inside <panel-list> by consumers. **panel-list.mjs never creates a separator itself:** it renders only a default <slot>. **Styled purely by a slotted rule:** matched via `::slotted(hr:not([hidden]))` in panel-list.css, using --panel-separator-color/--panel-separator-padding tokens, with no dedicated class or tagName of its own. Just place a plain <hr> inside <panel-list>, panel-list.mjs never creates a separator itself, this is real author-supplied light-DOM content matched by the ::slotted(hr:not([hidden])) rule. Don't look for a dedicated separator class or tagName, there isn't one, styling is entirely via --panel-separator-color/--panel-separator-padding on the plain <hr> itself. panel.separator.color panel.separator.padding.@base panel.separator.padding.block panel.separator.padding.inline

panel.title: panel
panel.text: A XUL popup panel used for menus, dropdowns, and arrow-anchored callouts. No JSDoc; wraps the native XULPopupElement and adds arrow-panel defaulting, animation lifecycle, and focus-restore behavior on top of it. <panel type="arrow" neverhidden="true"> <vbox class="panel-content">...</vbox> </panel> type The sole gate for arrow-panel behavior: "arrow" enables default flip/side/position/consumeoutsideclicks values, side auto-recalculation, and the panelopen/animate lifecycle. Any other value is a plain popup. flip Defaulted to "both" for arrow panels if unset; actual flip behavior is implemented natively by XULPopupElement, not in this file. side Defaulted to "top" for arrow panels; also recomputed dynamically to left/right/top/bottom by _setSideAttribute() on popuppositioned, based on alignmentPosition and text direction. position Defaulted to "bottomleft topleft" for arrow panels; positioning itself is implemented natively. consumeoutsideclicks Defaulted to "false" for arrow panels (arrow panels do NOT consume outside clicks by default). neverhidden When present, the shadow-root content slot is never forced to display:none on hide. no-open-on-anchor When present, skips toggling the open attribute on the anchor's root (toolbarbutton or .anchor-root) while the panel is shown. animate Opt out of open/close animation by setting to "false"; the component itself also writes "open"/"cancel" values as internal transition state. norestorefocus When set to "true", focus is not restored to the pre-open element after the panel closes. panelopen Read-only, state-reflecting: set true on popupshown and removed on popuphidden (arrow panels only). Consumers may select on it in CSS but should not set it. hidden Overridden getter/setter: setting hidden=false (or removing the attribute) lazily initializes the shadow DOM via ensureInitialized(). animating Internal-only transition lock, set true on popupshowing and removed on popupshown; not consumer-facing config. (default) Default shadow-DOM slot with part="content"; panel children render here. AlertActive Legacy Events-type event dispatched unconditionally from on_popupshown when event.target == this, for accessibility APIs. ensureInitialized panelContent Getter returning shadowRoot.querySelector('[part=content]'). content The default content slot (<html:slot part="content"/>), also returned by the panelContent getter. Rely on the automatic focus-restore behavior instead of tracking focus yourself, it already walks back through shadow roots to find and restore whatever had focus before the panel opened. Set neverhidden if content inside genuinely needs to stay laid out and measurable while the panel is closed. Don't treat hidden as a plain style toggle, its own setter lazily initializes the shadow DOM content the first time the panel is shown, so toggling it does real setup work. Don't hand-roll side or position math for an arrow panel, connectedCallback already defaults it for you unless you explicitly set your own values first. panel.background.color.@base panel.background.color.dimmed.@base panel.background.color.dimmed.further panel.border.color panel.border.radius panel.box.shadow.@base panel.box.shadow.margin panel.padding.@base panel.padding.block panel.separator.color panel.separator.padding.@base panel.separator.padding.block panel.separator.padding.inline panel.text.color panel.width popup.background.color popup.border.color popup.border.radius popup.box.shadow

popup-notification.title: popup-notification
popup-notification.text: A XUL widget rendering a single doorhanger notification (icon, origin, description, optional checkbox/warning/hint, close button, and primary/secondary moz-button pair) inside the panel managed by PopupNotifications.sys.mjs. **A light-DOM widget:** child elements are placed by tag-name lookup (querySelector) rather than native <slot> projection. <popupnotification popupid="geolocation" label="Share your location?" buttonlabel="Allow" secondarybuttonlabel="Block"> <popupnotificationcontent>...</popupnotificationcontent> </popupnotification> popupid Forwarded to the icon, body, and description parts; used to build data-l10n-id-style identifiers for the notification. icon Inherited as src on .popup-notification-icon. iconclass Inherited as an additional class on .popup-notification-icon. hasicon Inherited presence flag forwarded to .popup-notification-icon. origin Inherited as both the value and tooltiptext of the .popup-notification-origin link (the site/origin the notification is about). descriptionid Inherited as the id of .popup-notification-description. label Inherited as the first text span in the compound description sentence. name Inherited as the bold '.popup-notification-description-name' span (e.g. a site or permission name). endlabel Inherited as the second text span in the description. secondname Inherited as the trailing bold span in the description. secondendlabel Inherited as the final text span in the description. hinttext Inherited as the text of .popup-notification-hint-text, a secondary line below the main description. closebuttonhidden Inherited as hidden on the close toolbarbutton. learnmoreurl Inherited as href on the 'Learn more' link. warninghidden Inherited as hidden on the warning description. warninglabel Inherited as the text of the warning description. secondarybuttonlabel Inherited as the label of the secondary moz-button. secondarybuttonaccesskey Inherited as the accesskey of the secondary moz-button. secondarybuttonhidden Inherited as hidden on both the secondary button and the 'more actions' menupopup. buttonlabel Inherited as the label of the primary moz-button. buttonaccesskey Inherited as the accesskey of the primary moz-button. mainactiondisabled Inherited as disabled on the primary moz-button. dropmarkerhidden When present, forces the secondary button's type to "default" instead of "split" (hiding its chevron/menu affordance). popupnotificationheader Not a real <slot>: a child element with this tag name is moved into the header container above the icon/body row, if present. popupnotificationcontent Not a real <slot>: each child element with this tag name is appended before .popup-notification-bottom-content via appendNotificationContent(); repeatable. popupnotificationfooter Not a real <slot>: a child element with this tag name is moved into the footer container below the body, if present. buttoncommand Cancelable CustomEvent dispatched on primary-button click; if not canceled, forwarded to PopupNotifications._onButtonEvent. secondarybuttoncommand Cancelable CustomEvent dispatched on secondary-button click (when the click wasn't on the chevron); forwarded to PopupNotifications._onButtonEvent if not canceled. learnmoreclick Cancelable CustomEvent dispatched when the 'Learn more' link is clicked. show Lazily slots content (slotContents()) on first call, applies checkbox state, and un-hides the notification. appendNotificationContent appendNotificationContent(el): inserts an extra content element before the bottom-content box. --popup-notification-body-width Default width basis for the notification body and icon/body max-width calculations; defined globally in toolkit/themes/shared/global-shared.css, consumed in popupnotification.css. Use popupnotificationcontent for extra body content, appendNotificationContent() is real and repeatable, so more than one is fine. Set dropmarkerhidden when you want a plain secondary button, the secondary button defaults to a split-type chevron/menu affordance otherwise. Don't rely on native <slot> projection for popupnotificationheader/popupnotificationcontent/popupnotificationfooter children, they're matched by tag name via querySelector, not real slot assignment, so an unrelated element sharing one of those tag names would also get picked up. Don't assume buttoncommand/secondarybuttoncommand automatically do something, both are cancelable CustomEvents only forwarded to PopupNotifications._onButtonEvent if a listener doesn't cancel them first.

promo.title: promo
promo.text: A promotional callout element with an optional heading, image, actions and support link, and an optional dismiss button. <moz-promo heading="Try this feature" message="A short description of the feature." dismissable> <moz-button slot="actions">Get started</moz-button> </moz-promo> type The type of promo, either "default" or "vibrant". Determines the colors of the promotional element. heading The heading of the promo element. message The message of the promo element. imageSrc The main image of the promo element. imageAlignment How the image should be aligned. Can be "start", "end", or "center". imageWidth How big the image is sized. Can be "default", "small" or "large". imageDisplay Whether the image touches the edge of the promo or has a little padding around it. Can be "cover" or "padded". dismissable Whether the promo can be dismissed via a close button. actions Action controls (e.g. a moz-button) shown after the message. support-link A moz-support-link shown after the message/actions. promo:user-dismissed Fired when the promo is dismissed by the user via the close button. Cancelable; if defaultPrevented, the element does not remove itself. dismiss close Listen for the cancelable "promo:user-dismissed" event if you need to intercept dismissal, dismiss() only calls close()/remove() when the event isn't preventDefault()-ed. Don't expect imageAlignment="center" to get its own placement logic, render() only special-cases imageAlignment=="start" to put the image before the text; "center" and "end" are both placed after the text and rely on CSS alone for the visual difference. Don't set imageAlignment, imageWidth, or imageDisplay expecting a visible effect without also setting imageSrc, imageTemplate() only renders when imageSrc is truthy, so those reflected attributes are inert without it. moz-promo.background.color.@base moz-promo.background.color.vibrant moz-promo.border.@base moz-promo.border.color.@base moz-promo.border.color.vibrant moz-promo.border.radius moz-promo.border.width moz-promo.heading.text.color.@base moz-promo.heading.text.color.vibrant moz-promo.image.size.@base moz-promo.image.size.large moz-promo.message.text.color.@base moz-promo.message.text.color.vibrant moz-promo.padding

radio.title: radio
radio.text: Modern Lit-based radio group (moz-radio-group) that groups and associates moz-radio items so they function as a single form control. **A legacy XUL-style pair also exists** in the tree for older UI: <radiogroup>/<radio> (toolkit/content/widgets/radio.js, registered as tags "radiogroup" and "radio"). It implements roving-tabindex keyboard navigation (arrow keys, wrapping), a selectedItem/selectedIndex/value API, and dispatches a plain "select" event on selection, with attribute inheritance for disabled/selected/label/accesskey/crop/src. **The tables below describe the modern one:** moz-radio-group and its moz-radio children, which is the actively-recommended pair. <moz-radio-group label="Choose an option" name="example" value="1"> <moz-radio value="1" label="Option 1"></moz-radio> <moz-radio value="2" label="Option 2"></moz-radio> </moz-radio-group> disabled Whether or not the fieldset is disabled. label Label for the group of moz-radio elements. ariaLabel Accessible name for the group when no visible label is provided. description Description for the group of moz-radio elements. supportPage Support page for the group of moz-radio elements. headingLevel Render the label in a heading of this level. name Input name of the radio group. Propagates to moz-radio children. value Selected value for the group. Changing the value updates the checked state of moz-radio children and vice versa. (default) The radio group's content, intended for moz-radio elements. support-link The radio group's support link, intended to be associated with moz-radio elements. change Bubbles up from a selected moz-radio child; the group updates its value accordingly. fieldset The wrapping <fieldset>, inherited from SelectControlBaseElement (on the radio group, moz-radio-group.mjs). Set value on moz-radio-group rather than checked on individual moz-radio children, value is the single source of truth and its setter syncs every child's checked state and the form value for you. Remember moz-radio-group's constructor overrides orientation to "vertical", unlike sibling SelectControlBaseElement components (moz-segmented-control, moz-visual-picker) which keep the base "horizontal" default, so arrow-key navigation direction differs unless overridden. Don't nest moz-radio anywhere but as a direct child of moz-radio-group, the mixin's connectedCallback checks parentElement and logs "moz-radio can only be used in moz-radio-group element" if it isn't, so wrapping it breaks the association. Don't try to re-enable a single moz-radio by clearing its own disabled while the group stays disabled, isDisabled ORs in both parentDisabled and controller.parentDisabled, so the group's disabled state always wins (called out in the component's own docs).

reorderable-list.title: reorderable-list
reorderable-list.text:
A light wrapper that makes its slotted children (matched by itemSelector, or a narrower dragSelector for a drag handle) draggable and reorderable via native HTML5 drag-and-drop. **Consumers do the reordering, not the component:** it shows a drop-position indicator and dispatches dragstarted/dragended/reorder events carrying the dragged/target elements and computed indices; consumers perform the actual DOM reordering in response. **Keyboard reordering is opt-in:** it also exports a standalone isReorderKeyboardEvent(event) helper (ctrl+shift+up/down) for wiring an equivalent keyboard-driven reorder outside the component's own automatic handling.
  • One
  • Two
  • Three
    •  itemSelector Selector for slotted elements that should be reorderable. Reflected as the lowercase HTML attribute itemselector (no explicit attribute name is set on the property, so Lit uses its lowercased default). dragSelector Selector used when only part of a reorderable item should be the drag handle (e.g. a button or icon), instead of the whole item. Reflected as the lowercase HTML attribute dragselector. reorder Dispatched when an item is dropped in a new position. detail: { draggedElement, targetElement, position (-1 before / 0 after target), draggedIndex, targetIndex, insertAt }. dragstarted Dispatched when an item drag begins. detail: { draggedElement }. dragended Dispatched when a drag ends (drop or otherwise). detail: { draggedElement }. getItems Re-queries the assigned elements matching itemSelector, marks them draggable, and records their reorder indices; called on slotchange and DOM mutation. getAssignedElementsBySelector Returns all elements matching a selector among the given root elements (default: the default slot's assigned elements), recursing into shadow roots, children, and nested slots. getDropTargetInfo Computes the current drop target element, its index, and whether the drop is before/after it, based on the dragover/drop event position. getItemIndex Returns an item's recorded reorder index, or -1 if not tracked. getTargetItemFromEvent Finds the closest ancestor matching itemSelector for a given event's target. evaluateKeyDownEvent Given a keydown event, returns the reorder move it represents (dragged/target elements, indices) for ctrl+shift+up/down, or undefined if it isn't a reorder shortcut or there's nowhere to move. emitEvent Dispatches a CustomEvent with the given name and detail on the host element. addDraggableAttribute Sets the draggable attribute on non-XUL items so native drag-and-drop is enabled for them. isXULElement Reports whether a given element is a XUL element (which is draggable by default, unlike HTML elements). getBounds Returns an element's bounding rect, preferring the flush-free windowUtils API when available. onDragStart dragstart listener: identifies the dragged item, dispatches dragstarted, and (in privileged documents) builds a custom drag image. onDragOver dragover listener: computes and displays the drop-position indicator. onDragLeave dragleave listener: hides the drop-position indicator once the pointer truly leaves the list. onDrop drop listener: dispatches reorder (unless dropped on itself or into a no-op position) and cleans up. onDragEnd dragend listener (also called from onDrop): dispatches dragended and clears drag state. Perform the actual move yourself in a reorder listener, the element reports the drop and draws the indicator but never mutates the list. Use detail.insertAt rather than deriving an index from targetIndex and position, it already compensates for the left-shift of splicing the dragged item out of its old position. Call evaluateKeyDownEvent(event) from your own keydown handler for keyboard reordering, nothing calls it internally, and it returns the same detail shape as the reorder event or undefined when the move would be a no-op. Don't leave itemSelector unset unless your items really are
  • , the constructor defaults it to "li" and anything else is silently never made draggable. Don't treat reorder as firing on every drop, onDrop returns early when an item is dropped on itself or into an adjacent position that changes nothing, and only dragended fires in those cases. Don't read getItemIndex right after inserting items, onMutation defers getItems to the next requestAnimationFrame so the stamped indices are a frame stale.

segment.title: segment
segment.text: A single item within a moz-segmented-control, rendered as a button that can be selected. **Implemented as MozSegmentedControlItem,** which mixes SelectControlItemMixin into MozButton, in the same file as moz-segmented-control. **It is a real registered custom element:** the Acorn API's coverage table lists this tagName as null/unregistered, but the file does call customElements.define("moz-segmented-control-item", MozSegmentedControlItem). <moz-segmented-control-item value="list" label="List"></moz-segmented-control-item> label Label text for the button. value Value for this option. iconSrc Optional icon to display. checked Whether this item is selected. Internally toggles the underlying moz-button's type between "primary" (checked) and "ghost" (unchecked). disabled Whether this item is disabled. parentDisabled Set by the parent moz-segmented-control when it is disabled. size Button size, "default" or "small". accessKey Access key for keyboard shortcut. ariaLabel Accessible label when no visible label is present. input Manually dispatched (bubbles, composed) on click, since the item is not backed by a native input. Not dispatched when the item is disabled or already checked, since handleClick returns before dispatching. change Manually dispatched (bubbles, composed) on click, alongside input. Not dispatched when the item is disabled or already checked, since handleClick returns before dispatching. Always set both value and label, the parent moz-segmented-control needs value for identity and label for display, neither is optional in real usage. Listen for the real input/change events for selection handling, the item isn't backed by a native input and manually dispatches both on click. Don't use this component outside a real moz-segmented-control parent, size and parentDisabled are explicitly set by that parent, there's no standalone usage documented. Don't expect accessKey to show a visible hint on its own, it wires a real keyboard shortcut but any visible indicator is the parent's concern, not this item's.

segmented-control.title: segmented-control
segmented-control.text: A segmented control that groups moz-segmented-control-item children and lets a user switch between them, functioning as either a tab switcher (when wired to a named-deck via the deck attribute) or a radio button group. **It inherits more than its own JSDoc documents:** it extends the shared SelectControlBaseElement, so it also gets label, description, name, and orientation handling from that base class even though this subclass's own JSDoc only documents deck/value/name/disabled. <moz-segmented-control value="list"> <moz-segmented-control-item value="list" label="List"></moz-segmented-control-item> <moz-segmented-control-item value="grid" label="Grid"></moz-segmented-control-item> </moz-segmented-control> deck Optional ID of a named-deck to control for tab switching. value Currently selected value. name Form control name. disabled Whether the control is disabled. (default) The control's items, intended for moz-segmented-control-item children. change Bubbles up from a selected child item; the control updates its value and (if deck is set) switches the linked named-deck's view. fieldset The wrapping <fieldset>, inherited from SelectControlBaseElement. Set deck to the id of a named-deck that shares the same root node as the moz-segmented-control, setupDeckListener() only calls getRootNode().querySelector(), so a deck living in a different shadow root silently fails to wire up with no error. Don't expect items to get role="tab" just because the control looks like a tab switcher, getChildRole() only returns "tab" when a deck attribute is actually set; without it items stay role="radio" regardless of visual usage. Don't rely on a native input/change event.target being an <input>, moz-segmented-control-item isn't a real form input, handleClick() manually dispatches synthetic bubbling input and change events from the button element itself. moz-segmented-control.border.@base moz-segmented-control.border.color moz-segmented-control.border.radius moz-segmented-control.padding

select.title: select
select.text: A select dropdown whose options are provided as moz-option light-DOM children. Renders a native <select> when no options have icons, or a panel-list/button combo when at least one moz-option has an icon. <moz-select label="Search engine" name="search-engine" value="option1"> <moz-option value="option1" label="Option 1"></moz-option> <moz-option value="option2" label="Option 2"></moz-option> </moz-select> label The text of the label element. size The select size. Options: `default`, `small`. name The name of the input control. value The value of the selected option. disabled The disabled state of the input control. iconSrc The src for an optional icon. description Text for the description element that helps describe the input control. supportPage Name of the SUMO support page to link to. ariaLabel The aria-label text when there is no visible label. ariaDescription The aria-description text when there is no visible description. title The title attribute, mapped onto the inner control. options Internal reactive state (state: true, not reflected): array of options read from <moz-option> children. selectedOption Internal reactive state (state: true, not reflected): the currently selected option object. selectedIndex Internal reactive state (state: true, not reflected): index of the currently selected option. usePanelList Internal reactive state (state: true, not reflected): whether to render the panel-list/button combo instead of a native <select>, true when at least one option has an icon. (default) moz-option (and <hr> separator) children that populate the select's options. Read via MutationObserver, not meant to be styled directly. change Redispatched when the selected value changes, whether via the native <select> or the panel-list path. Let updated() auto-wire panelTrigger.popoverTargetElement to the panel-list whenever usePanelList is true, you don't need to set the popover target yourself. Explicitly set a valid value when any moz-option has an iconSrc, populateOptions() only auto-defaults to the first option to mimic native <select> behavior in that panel-list mode; the plain <select> fallback relies on the browser's own default selection instead. Don't assume mixing icon-less and icon-bearing moz-option children keeps the native <select> rendering, usePanelList flips the whole control to the panel-list/button combobox the moment any single option has an iconSrc. Don't expect ArrowUp/ArrowDown to behave the same across platforms once usePanelList is active, handlePanelKeydown() opens the panel on Mac but directly changes the selection via selectNextOption() on Windows/Linux, per navigator.platform checks (see also the Mac-only focus workaround in handlePanelMousedown for Bug 2017668). moz-select.background.color.@base moz-select.background.color.disabled moz-select.background.color.hover moz-select.border.@base moz-select.border.color.@base moz-select.border.color.disabled moz-select.border.color.hover moz-select.border.radius moz-select.font.size.@base moz-select.font.size.small moz-select.font.weight moz-select.icon.fill moz-select.min.height.@base moz-select.min.height.small moz-select.opacity.disabled moz-select.option.font.weight moz-select.option.text.color moz-select.padding.block moz-select.padding.icon moz-select.space.inline.@base moz-select.space.inline.small moz-select.text.color.@base moz-select.text.color.disabled moz-select.text.color.hover

sidebar-panel.title: sidebar-panel
sidebar-panel.text: Per-panel header for a sidebar panel, showing the panel title and a close button, plus each panel's own toolbar content (search boxes, options menus, etc.) via its default slot. In horizontal-tabs "hide-launcher" mode the title is replaced by the sidebar-panel-switcher dropdown, since there is no launcher to switch panels with. <sidebar-panel-header view="viewBookmarksSidebar" heading="Bookmarks"></sidebar-panel-header> view The view id of the panel this header belongs to; forwarded to the internal close moz-button and the sidebar-panel-switcher. heading The panel title text rendered in the header. (default) Each panel's own toolbar content (search boxes, options menus, etc.), rendered below the heading row. Reach the outer browser window the same way getWindow() does (window.browsingContext.embedderWindowGlobal.browsingContext.window) rather than assuming this document's own window has SidebarController, since this header typically renders in an embedded document. Don't assume the close button always reveals the launcher, closeSidebarPanel's dismissPanel flag is computed from controller._state.launcherHiddenWithPanel, in hide-launcher mode it keeps the panel remembered instead of dismissing it since there's no launcher to return to.

sidebar-strip.title: sidebar-strip
sidebar-strip.text: Sidebar launcher strip with expanded and collapsed states that provides entry points to various sidebar panels and sidebar extensions, plus bottom actions like "Customize sidebar". Default export SidebarMain, registered as custom element sidebar-main. expanded Reflected attribute; whether the launcher strip is in its expanded (labelled, vertical-tabs) state versus collapsed icon-only state. selectedView The view id of the currently selected/open sidebar panel; initialized from window.SidebarController.currentID. open Whether the sidebar is currently open; initialized from window.SidebarController.isOpen. bottomActions Internal list of bottom action entries (e.g. "Customize sidebar"), populated by setCustomize(). sidebarItems Declared in static properties but not read or written anywhere else in the file; appears to be unused/vestigial in the current implementation. shouldShowOverflowButton Internal computed state controlling visibility of the tools overflow ("more tools") button. isOverflowMenuOpen Internal state tracking whether the tools overflow popup menu is open. tabstrip Slot for the tab strip content (used in vertical-tabs mode). sidebar-contextmenu-ready Dispatched on the host after the sidebar context menu has finished being populated asynchronously (see onSidebarPopupShowing). Expect requestUpdate() to have effect only while the sidebar is visible, shouldUpdate() unconditionally returns false when the sidebar container's hidden is true, so property changes made while hidden won't render until it's shown again. Don't treat getEntrypointValues(action) as a pure read, for the GenAI chat entry it mutates the passed-in action object's iconUrl and tooltiptext in place, rewriting data on the shared SidebarController.toolsAndExtensions action rather than just local render state. Don't rely on Lit's reactivity for the overflow-panel's copy buttons, they're plain DOM clones created in createCopyButton because "Lit will lose the original references," so any state change not followed by an explicit resetPanelButtonValues() call leaves their aria-pressed/type stale.

sidebar.title: sidebar
sidebar.text: SidebarController is a plain singleton object (var SidebarController = {...}), not a class or custom element; it manages sidebar panel visibility/toggling, builds the View > Sidebar menu items, tracks per-tool notification badges, and exposes the sidebar API used by extensions. Treat SidebarController as the single real source of truth for visibility, toggling, and the View > Sidebar menu, it's a plain singleton object, not a class you instantiate per sidebar instance. Don't build a separate subsystem for per-tool notification badges, SidebarController itself tracks and exposes them alongside visibility state. sidebar.background.color sidebar.border.color sidebar.text.color

split-button.title: split-button
split-button.text: Two separately-implemented split-button-shaped patterns exist at once, not one. **Classic:** a customized-built-in element registered as plain <button> (customElements.define("button", MozButton), toolkit/content/widgets/button.js), where type="menu" renders a .button-menu-dropmarker fragment alongside icon+label (MozButton.menuFragment) with a <menupopup> child, used in historySidebar.xhtml, customizeMode.inc.xhtml, and others. **Modern:** <moz-button type="split">, a mode of moz-button already documented under the "button" component (its own type variant list includes "split"). **Not the implementation:** toolkit/content/widgets/toolbarbutton.js has no menu-button/split rendering branch (only plain icon+label and a badged icon+label, no dropmarker), so it is not the split-button implementation; <button> (this entry) is. <button type="menu" label="View"> <menupopup>...</menupopup> </button> <!-- classic dropmarker split button (button.js, class MozButton). --> <!-- for the modern equivalent, see <moz-button type="split"> under the "button" component --> type On classic <button>: "menu" renders the real dropmarker split-button fragment (MozButton.menuFragment). Other classic values (checkbox, radio) are unrelated modes of the same MozButtonBase class, not split-button variants. label Classic <button>'s visible text; inherited onto .button-text along with accesskey and crop (static inheritedAttributes). image Path to the icon image; inherited onto .button-icon's src (inheritedAttributes: "src=image"). disabled Classic <button>'s disabled state, reflected via MozButtonBase and inherited onto the dropmarker too. open Reflects/controls the associated <menupopup>'s open state via hasMenu()/openMenu(). icon Getter: this.querySelector(".button-icon"), the classic <button>'s icon image element. --button-gap-split Gap between the main action and the chevron, on the modern <moz-button type="split">. --button-border-width-split Border width of the inner divider between the main action and the chevron, on the modern <moz-button type="split">. --button-split-separator-background-color Color of the divider line between the main action and the chevron, on the modern <moz-button type="split">. Use <moz-button type="split"> for new code, it's the modern, actively-maintained implementation; the classic <button type="menu"> still ships and works but is the older pattern. Always pair the classic type="menu" with a real <menupopup> child, open()/hasMenu() depend on one actually being present. Don't cite toolbarbutton.js as a split-button implementation, it has no menu-button/split rendering branch at all, only plain icon+label and a badged icon+label. Don't expect the classic dropmarker fragment to render for type="checkbox" or type="radio", those are unrelated modes of the same MozButtonBase class, not split-button variants. button.border.width.split button.gap.split button.split.separator.background.color

spotlight-modal.title: spotlight-modal
spotlight-modal.text: Spotlight is a plain exported object (export const Spotlight = {...}), not a class or custom element. **What it opens:** ASRouter/onboarding 'spotlight' messages as an HTML dialog (chrome://browser/content/spotlight.html) rendered either tab-modal or window-modal, via the browser's tab dialog box or gDialogBox. await Spotlight.showSpotlightDialog(browser, { content: { modal: "tab" }, trigger: { id: "defaultBrowserCheck" }, }); message.content.modal "tab" opens the dialog tab-modal via gBrowser's tab dialog box; any other value (or omitted) opens it window-modal via gDialogBox. message.content.metrics "block" suppresses IMPRESSION/DISMISS telemetry dispatch and CFR action dispatch for this message. message.content.write_in_microsurvey When true, added to the telemetry event_context for user-event telemetry. message.trigger.id When "lastWindowClose", replaces any already-open dialog and aborts other tab dialogs on the selected browser so this modal takes priority before the window closes. showSpotlightDialog async showSpotlightDialog(browser, message, dispatch = defaultDispatch): opens the dialog for the given message; returns a Promise<boolean> resolving once the dialog is closed (false if it couldn't be opened). close close(window?): closes the open dialog if no window is given, or if the given window owns it. isOpen Getter: whether a spotlight dialog is currently open. sendUserEventTelemetry sendUserEventTelemetry(event, message, dispatch): dispatches a SPOTLIGHT_TELEMETRY action for IMPRESSION/DISMISS events (skipped when message.content.metrics === "block"). defaultDispatch defaultDispatch(message): default dispatch handler, forwards SPOTLIGHT_TELEMETRY messages to AboutWelcomeTelemetry. Check the boolean returned by showSpotlightDialog() before assuming the dialog displayed, it returns false without opening anything when win.gDialogBox.isOpen is already true (the lastWindowClose trigger is the sole exception, which force-replaces/aborts existing dialogs first). Remember _dialog/_dialogWindow are module-level singleton state, not per-window, so Spotlight.isOpen and the open-check in showSpotlightDialog() apply across all browser windows, not just the one calling it. Don't call Spotlight.close(window) from a window other than the one that opened the dialog expecting it to close, close() only acts when no window is passed or when window strictly matches the stored _dialogWindow. Don't expect IMPRESSION/DISMISS telemetry to fire when message.content.metrics === "block", sendUserEventTelemetry() bails out immediately and dispatchCFRAction becomes a no-op for that message.

stepper.title: stepper
stepper.text: MultiStageProtonScreen (function component) and ProtonScreen (React.PureComponent it renders) implement one step of the multi-screen stepper-style onboarding flow used by about:welcome, Spotlight, and FeatureCallout tours. **What one step renders:** the step-progress indicator (StepsIndicator or ProgressBar), title/subtitle, hero image/tiles, and action buttons for the current screen's content config. **A real React implementation,** not a custom element. <MultiStageProtonScreen content={screenContent} id={screenContent.id} order={order} totalNumberOfScreens={screens.length} handleAction={handleAction} navigate={navigate} /> content Required per-screen config, read directly in ProtonScreen.render(): title, subtitle, position ("center"|"split"|"callout"|...), background/background_static, hero_image, tiles, primary_button/secondary_button/additional_button, dismiss_button, checkbox, progress_bar, steps_indicator, logo, narrow, fullscreen, zap_border, zap_shadow, video_container, cta_paragraph, info_text, languageSwitcher, and more. id Screen id, used as a CSS class on the rendered <main>. order Zero-based index of this screen; used for the steps indicator's current-step count and to alternate the screen-1/screen-2 background class. totalNumberOfScreens Total screen count, used by the steps indicator. previousOrder Order of the previously shown screen; used for step-transition numbering and to detect the very first screen shown. handleAction Callback invoked by buttons/checkbox/tiles with a synthetic event-like object carrying a `value` naming which content-tree action to take. navigate Advances or dismisses the tour; called directly by MultiStageProtonScreen's own auto-advance effect. autoAdvance Optional; when set, MultiStageProtonScreen calls handleAction automatically after a timeout (autoAdvance.actionTimeMS, default 20000ms). advanceOnExperimentLoad Optional; alternative to autoAdvance: waits for window.AWWaitForNimbus() (bounded by minDisplayMs/maxDisplayMs) then calls navigate(false). isFirstScreen Affects the dialog-initial CSS class. isLastScreen Affects the dialog-last CSS class. isSingleScreen When true, hides the steps indicator. requireAction When true, focuses the title heading on mount instead of the main content container, and makes the title focusable. ariaRole Role for the rendered <main>; defaults to "alertdialog". forceHideStepsIndicator Forces the steps indicator to be hidden regardless of other conditions. aboveButtonStepsIndicator Renders the steps indicator above the action buttons instead of at the end of main content. animationsPaused Swaps animated background/hero-image assets for their _static counterparts, and reflects a pressed play/pause toggle. toggleAnimationsPaused Callback for the animation play/pause button. isRtamo, addonId, addonType, addonName, addonURL, addonIconURL, themeScreenshots, installedAddons Props for the 'return to AMO' addon-install flow, used to render an install button/icon in place of the normal primary action. messageId Destructured directly in the MultiStageProtonScreen function component's own top-level props (separately from the content-config props it forwards to ProtonScreen). isWideScreen Read in ProtonScreen.render(); affects layout for wide-viewport presentations. When using a progress_bar screen, know that ProgressBar's useEffect has an intentionally empty dependency array (eslint-disabled) so it only recalculates progress on mount, relying on the whole screen remounting a fresh ProgressBar instance on every step change rather than the same instance re-rendering. Don't assume the steps indicator always renders in one place, ProtonScreen.render() calls renderStepsIndicator() from up to three different spots depending on aboveButtonStepsIndicator, content.progress_bar, and content.fullscreen. Don't expect a steps indicator to render at all when autoAdvance, content.video_container, isSingleScreen, or forceHideStepsIndicator is set, hideStepsIndicator ORs all four together unconditionally. Don't set both autoAdvance and advanceOnExperimentLoad expecting them to combine, the effect checks autoAdvance first, so if it's truthy, advanceOnExperimentLoad's min/max-display-time and Nimbus-wait logic never runs at all.

support-link.title: support-link
support-link.text: A customized built-in for linking to Mozilla's SUMO support documentation. Its class extends StylesMixin(HTMLAnchorElement, styles), so it is a subclass of HTMLAnchorElement that also adopts moz-support-link.css onto its root. **It builds its own href** from a support-page short-hand plus the app's support base URL (the app.support.baseURL pref), optionally appending AMO-only UTM parameters via utm-content, and always opens in a new tab/window via openTrustedLinkIn. **It fills its own localized text** via Fluent when no content or data-l10n-id is supplied. support-page Short-hand string identifying the specific SUMO support page; combined with the app's support base URL to build href. Also exposed as the supportPage JS property. utm-content UTM content parameter appended to the URL, only applied when the resulting URL is an AMO (mozilla.org/allizom.org) URL. data-l10n-id Fluent id used to generate the link's text content when none is otherwise provided. Give it a data-l10n-id or a real element child when you want your own link text, connectedCallback substitutes the default "moz-support-link-text" string whenever there is no l10n id and childElementCount is 0, so a plain text node gets replaced. Reserve it for SUMO pages, its own JSDoc says other "Learn more" links should use a plain anchor element. Don't set href yourself, #setHref rebuilds it from the app's support base URL on connect and again on every support-page or utm-content change, overwriting whatever you assigned. Don't assume a click follows the href normally in chrome, handleEvent calls preventDefault and routes through openTrustedLinkIn, rewriting a "current" destination to "tab".

tab-group.title: tab-group
tab-group.text: A named, colorable, collapsible container that groups related tabs (and split-view wrappers) together in the tabstrip. A classic XUL custom element with a static light-DOM template (label + overflow-count areas) and no shadow root. <tab-group id="group-1" label="Research" color="blue"> <tab is="tabbrowser-tab"/> <tab is="tabbrowser-tab"/> </tab-group> label The group's display name; setter falls back to a zero-width space so layout stays stable, updates aria/tooltip, and fires TabGroupUpdate on change. Aliased as "name". collapsed Whether the group's tabs are collapsed/hidden; setter unlocks tab widths, updates aria/tooltip/overflow, and fires TabGroupCollapse/TabGroupExpand. color Not attribute-backed: the setter writes six CSS custom properties (--tab-group-color, -color-invert, -color-pale, -background-color, -background-color-hover, -text-color, -text-color-invert) pointing at the matching palette token set. Valid values: blue, cyan, gray, green, orange, pink, purple, red, yellow. hasactivetab Reflects whether one of the group's member tabs is currently active; updated in response to TabSelect/SplitViewTabChange. movingtabgroup Internal drag/drop coordination flag, backed by the isBeingDragged getter/setter. previewpanelactive Internal flag for the hover-preview panel, gated behind the browser.tabs.groups.hoverPreview.enabled pref. hasmultipletabs Internal CSS hook toggled by #updateOverflowLabel() to control overflow-count display. (default) Real children (tab and tab-split-view-wrapper elements) are always inserted, via an overridden appendChild, immediately before the overflow-count container, giving DOM order [label-container, ...tabs/split-views..., overflow-count-container]. There is no shadow root, so the <html:slot/> in the static markup is a positional placeholder only, not a functioning slot. TabGroupCreate Fired once in connectedCallback on first mount; detail: {isAdoptingGroup} when created via adoption. TabGroupUpdate Fired from the color and label setters whenever the value actually changes. TabGroupRemoved Fired by a mutation observer when the group's tab count hits 0, just before the group removes itself. TabGroupCollapse Fired from the collapsed setter when collapsing. TabGroupExpand Fired from the collapsed setter when expanding. TabGroupAnimationComplete Fired after all pending member-tab width-transition animations settle following a collapse/expand. TabGroupUngroup Fired at the start of ungroupTabs(); detail: {metricsContext}. TabGroupSaved Fired in save() after the group is added to SessionStore as a saved tab group; detail: {metricsContext}. TabGroupLabelHoverStart Dispatched on the internal label element (not the host) on mouseover. TabGroupLabelHoverEnd Dispatched on the internal label element (not the host) on mouseout. addTabs ungroupTabs save saveAndClose isTabVisibleInGroup select appendChild --tab-group-label-size Font size of the group label. --tab-group-label-container-size Size of the label container. --tab-group-counter-size Size of the overflow-count label. --tab-group-label-height Height of the label. --tab-group-label-padding Padding of the label. --tab-group-label-highlight-thickness Thickness of the label's hover/active highlight. --tab-group-label-highlight-radius Border radius of the label's hover/active highlight (horizontal tabstrip; 4px for vertical). --tab-group-label-hover-inset Inset of the label hover highlight (vertical tabstrip only). --tab-group-label-animation-duration Duration of label-related animations. --tab-group-line-thickness Thickness of the colored context line under grouped tabs. --tab-group-line-toolbar-border-distance Distance of the context line from the toolbar border. --tab-group-line-color Color of the context line. --tab-group-{color} Per-color palette base token; color is one of blue, cyan, gray, green, orange, pink, purple, red, yellow. --tab-group-{color}-hover Per-color hover variant. --tab-group-{color}-invert Per-color inverted variant. --tab-group-{color}-text Per-color text variant. --tab-group-{color}-text-invert Per-color inverted text variant. --tab-group-{color}-pale Per-color pale/muted variant. --dragover-tab-group-color Drag-feedback color, set by drag-and-drop.js and consumed in tabs.css. Read back an empty group name expecting a zero-width space character, not an empty string, the label setter deliberately writes label || "\u200b" "so we always create a text node and get consistent layout." Don't toggle the collapsed attribute directly instead of setting the collapsed property, the property setter is what unlocks locked tab max-widths, updates aria attributes/tooltip/overflow label, deactivates the hover-preview panel, and fires TabGroupCollapse/Expand events, none of which run if you bypass it. Don't assume appendChild adds to the very end, it's overridden to always insertBefore the tab-group-overflow-count-container sentinel, so hand-appended content ends up before that overflow counter. tab.group.blue.@base tab.group.blue.hover tab.group.blue.invert tab.group.blue.text.@base tab.group.blue.text.invert tab.group.cyan.@base tab.group.cyan.hover tab.group.cyan.invert tab.group.cyan.text.@base tab.group.cyan.text.invert tab.group.gray.@base tab.group.gray.hover tab.group.gray.invert tab.group.gray.text.@base tab.group.gray.text.invert tab.group.green.@base tab.group.green.hover tab.group.green.invert tab.group.green.text.@base tab.group.green.text.invert tab.group.orange.@base tab.group.orange.hover tab.group.orange.invert tab.group.orange.text.@base tab.group.orange.text.invert tab.group.pink.@base tab.group.pink.hover tab.group.pink.invert tab.group.pink.text.@base tab.group.pink.text.invert tab.group.purple.@base tab.group.purple.hover tab.group.purple.invert tab.group.purple.text.@base tab.group.purple.text.invert tab.group.red.@base tab.group.red.hover tab.group.red.invert tab.group.red.text.@base tab.group.red.text.invert tab.group.yellow.@base tab.group.yellow.hover tab.group.yellow.invert tab.group.yellow.text.@base tab.group.yellow.text.invert

tab-split.title: tab-split
tab-split.text: A wrapper that holds exactly two tabs shown side-by-side in a split view. A classic XUL custom element with no internal template or shadow root; its only real content is the two wrapped <tab> elements. <tab-split-view-wrapper splitViewId="1"> <tab is="tabbrowser-tab"/> <tab is="tabbrowser-tab"/> </tab-split-view-wrapper> hasactivetab Reflects whether one of the two wrapped tabs is currently active; drives internal activate()/suspend() behavior. multiselected Get-only in this file; set externally by multi-select code elsewhere. splitViewId Mixed-case attribute holding a numeric session-restore identity for the split view, exposed via the state getter. hidden Toggled based on the visible getter; watched by the element's own subtree MutationObserver. dragtarget External-only hook: referenced in tabs.css for drag styling but never set or read inside this file; managed by drag-and-drop code elsewhere. (default) Exactly two tab elements (the two tabs being viewed side-by-side), added/removed via addTabs()/unsplitTabs()/replaceTab(). No static template or shadow DOM. SplitViewTabChange Dispatched on this element (bubbles) from a mutation-observer callback whenever the child-tab composition changes and at least one tab remains. tab-group.js listens for this event. SplitViewRemoved Dispatched on this.container (gBrowser.tabContainer), bubbles and composed, in disconnectedCallback. TabSplitViewActivate Dispatched on this.container; detail: {tabs, splitview: this}; fired from the private #activate() method. TabSplitViewDeactivate Dispatched on this.container; detail: {tabs, splitview: this}; fired from both real teardown (#deactivate()) and temporary hide-while-switching (#suspend()); the same event name covers both cases. addTabs unsplitTabs trigger values: menu_separate | icon_separate | icon_close | tab_close | footer_separate replaceTab reverseTabs close resetRightPanelWidth --split-view-padding-block Block padding of the split view (default 2px), set in tabs.css. --split-view-tab-padding-inline Inline padding of each split-view tab (default 2px), set in tabs.css. Let the tab-change MutationObserver call unsplitTabs("tab_close") automatically when a split view is reduced to one tab, there's no need to call it yourself after removing a tab since the observer detects the single-tab case and moves the remaining tab out for you. Don't include a pinned tab in the array passed to addTabs(), the per-tab loop does "if (tab.pinned) return" which aborts the entire call as soon as it reaches a pinned tab, silently leaving any tabs already processed before it in place while dropping the rest. Don't assume more than two tabs are handled uniformly, resetRightPanelWidth() only ever operates on this.panels[1], hardcoding a two-panel structure even though addTabs technically allows arbitrary counts.

tab.title: tab
tab.text: A single browser tab: icon, title label, audio/sharing/note indicators, and close button. A customized built-in element extending the toolkit <tab> element (is="tabbrowser-tab"); builds its light-DOM structure once from a static template and drives it via an attribute-inheritance map. <tab is="tabbrowser-tab" label="Example Domain" pinned usercontextid="1" soundplaying="true"></tab> pinned Whether the tab is pinned to the start of the tabstrip. selected Whether the tab is the active tab; set via the internal _selected setter, actual selection is driven by gBrowser. multiselected Whether the tab is part of a multi-selection. muted Whether audio playback on the tab is muted. soundplaying Whether the tab is currently playing audio. pictureinpicture Whether the tab has an active picture-in-picture window. activemedia-blocked Whether autoplay media on the tab was blocked. usercontextid The container (contextual identity) id the tab belongs to. undiscardable Whether the tab is protected from automatic memory-saving discard. attention Whether the tab is showing an attention dot (e.g. a background alert). label The tab's title text, inherited onto the internal .tab-label element. tab-note Whether the tab has an attached note, backed by the hasTabNote getter/setter. visuallyselected Internal e10s tab-switch visual state, distinct from logical selection. busy Internal loading-state flag driving the throbber. bursting Internal flag driving the throbber's completion "burst" animation. textoverflow Internal CSS hook for label text-overflow fade direction. soundplaying-scheduledremoval Internal grace-period flag before the sound icon is removed; drives --soundplaying-removal-delay. customizemode Internal state reflecting whether the browser is in toolbar customize mode. TabHoverStart Bubbling Event dispatched from an internal mouseenter handler when the pointer enters the tab. TabHoverEnd Bubbling Event dispatched from an internal mouseleave handler. TabNoteIconHoverStart Bubbling CustomEvent with detail {noteIconElement}, dispatched when the pointer enters the tab-note icon. TabNoteIconHoverEnd Bubbling CustomEvent with detail {returningToTab}, dispatched when the pointer leaves the tab-note icon. TabGrouped Bubbling CustomEvent dispatched on the tab's new tab-group (detail: the tab) when the tab newly belongs to that group. TabUngrouped Bubbling CustomEvent dispatched on the tab-group being left (detail: the tab) when the tab leaves it. initialize updateLastAccessed updateLastSeenActive updateLastUnloadedByTabUnloader recordTimeFromUnloadToReload resumeDelayedMedia toggleMuteAudio registerAudibleChangeHandler unregisterAudibleChangeHandler setUserContextId updateA11yDescription updateSplitViewAriaLabel --tab-background-color-hover Background color on hover. --tab-background-color-selected Background color when selected. --tab-border-radius Tab border radius. --tab-border-color-accent Accent border color (e.g. for group color). --tab-border-color-selected-leading Leading-edge border color when selected. --tab-border-color-selected-trailing Trailing-edge border color when selected. --tab-box-shadow-selected Box shadow when selected. --tab-close-button-padding Padding around the close button. --tab-hover-outline-color Outline color on hover. --tab-selected-outline-color Outline color when selected. --tab-selected-textcolor Text color when selected. --tab-selected-color-scheme Color scheme when selected. --tab-outline Default outline. --tab-outline-color Default outline toolbar.text: The real XUL <toolbar> element. **Not Lit and not a registered custom element:** <toolbar> is a built-in XUL tag with no dedicated JS class, which is why navigator-toolbox.js delegates events on the outer #navigator-toolbox container rather than on any individual toolbar. **Its configuration is still real and citable:** navigator-toolbox.inc.xhtml declares five of them (toolbar-menubar, TabsToolbar, nav-bar, PersonalToolbar, notifications-toolbar) carrying attributes CustomizableUI reads to decide whether an area is customizable, where widgets actually land, and how overflow behaves. customizable Presence-only. Attach real interactive behavior at the outer toolbox container level, not per individual <toolbar>, that's how navigator-toolbox.js's own event delegation actually works. Treat nav-bar, PersonalToolbar, and TabsToolbar as the same real pattern, events just bubble up from buttons inside them to one shared container listener. Don't look for a distinct "toolbar" implementation separate from "toolbox", there isn't one in this file, it's the same underlying event delegation either way. toolbar.background.color toolbar.field.background.color.@base toolbar.field.background.color.focus toolbar.field.border.color.@base toolbar.field.border.color.focus toolbar.field.text.color.@base toolbar.field.text.color.focus toolbar.padding.inline toolbar.text.color

urlbar-action.text: Plain markup created by UrlbarView.mjs (a JS class, not a custom element). **Two shapes:** a `.urlbarView-action` span holding the inline action label (e.g. "Search with Google") shown within a result row, or a `.urlbarView-action-btn` secondary-action button created by #createSecondaryAction (e.g. switch-to-tab, pin, dismiss). **Distinct from the row itself,** which is the 'urlbar-result' concept. urlbar-identity.text: gIdentityHandler is a plain singleton object (var gIdentityHandler = {...}), not a class or custom element. **What it does:** it computes and renders the site identity/security state (lock icon, identity box label, permission indicators) for the current page, and handles clicks/keypresses on those icons in the url bar. Route all site-identity/security-state UI (lock icon, identity box label, permission indicators) through gIdentityHandler, it's the one real singleton computing and rendering all of it together. Don't wire up clicks/keypresses on these icons separately, gIdentityHandler already owns that interaction.

urlbar-result.text: Plain `.urlbarView-row` divs (role=option) created by UrlbarView.mjs (a JS class, not a custom element) via #createRowContent/#createRowContentForRichSuggestion/etc. **One row is one result:** each row represents one full search/suggestion result in the dropdown, and can contain an 'urlbar-action' label or button as a sub-element. **So result and action are related but distinct concepts** in this file: result is the row, action is a piece within it. Remember a real result row can contain a urlbar-action (a label or button) as a sub-element, they're related but distinct concepts in UrlbarView.mjs. urlbar.title: urlbar
urlbar.text: The browser's address bar input. It wraps a plain <input> and drives search mode, autofill, and the results view (UrlbarView). **Classic despite the moz- prefix,** which predates the modern naming convention: this is a classic custom element with no JSDoc/Lit conventions. **The tag and the implementation live in different files:** UrlbarInput.mjs now only registers the moz-urlbar tag on a thin subclass (`export class UrlbarInput extends UrlbarInputBase {}`), and the real implementation lives in the sibling UrlbarInputBase.mjs. <moz-urlbar id="urlbar-input" sap-name="urlbar" pageproxystate="valid"></moz-urlbar> sap-name Which surface this instance represents: "urlbar", "searchbar", or "smartbar"; backed by the sapName getter. pageproxystate "valid" when the displayed value matches the loaded page URL, "invalid" once the user starts typing/searching; gates autofill and search-mode behavior. open Observed attribute; reflects whether the results view (breakout/expanded state) is open. Toggled by UrlbarView. focused Reflects focus state on the container for styling purposes. actiontype Reflects a result's action type when autofilling a suggestion. textoverflow "start" or "end"; controls which side the value text-overflow fade appears on. searchmode Present while a search mode (e.g. a specific search engine or local scope) is active; removed on exit. persistsearchterms Controls whether search terms persist in the input after a search is performed. action-override Internal override used to force a specific action/result type. readOnly JS getter/setter property (not a plain attribute) that reflects to the underlying input field's readOnly state. remote-control-box Bespoke slot (via urlbar-slot="remote-control-box" on a child, moved by #populateSlots) shown when the browser is remotely controlled. site-info Bespoke slot for site identity/permissions info shown before the input. revert-button Bespoke slot for the button that reverts a typed value back to the page URL. page-actions Bespoke slot for page action buttons shown after the input (e.g. star/bookmark, extensions). search-one-offs Bespoke slot for the one-off search engine buttons shown in the results view. beforefocus Cancelable CustomEvent fired before focus() proceeds. beforeselect Cancelable CustomEvent fired before select()/setSelectionRange() proceeds. SetURI Bubbling CustomEvent fired on the input field after setURI() updates the displayed value. ValueChange Legacy accessibility event fired when the value changes. searchmodechanged Bubbling Event fired whenever a search mode is entered or exited. focus blur select setSelectionRange setURI search startQuery handleCommand handleNavigation handleRevert handoff pickResult getSearchMode setSearchMode getSearchSource setPageProxyState formatValue updatePlaceholder setUnifiedSearchButtonAvailability --urlbar-background-color Background color of the urlbar. --urlbar-background-color-focus Background color when the urlbar is focused. --urlbar-border-radius Border radius of the urlbar. --urlbar-box-background-color Background color of the input box. --urlbar-box-background-color-hover Background color of the input box on hover. --urlbar-box-background-color-active Background color of the input box while active. --urlbar-box-background-color-focus Background color of the input box while focused. --urlbar-box-text-color Text color inside the input box. --urlbar-box-text-color-hover Text color inside the input box on hover. --urlbar-icon-fill-opacity Fill opacity applied to icons inside the urlbar. --urlbar-margin-inline Inline margin around the urlbar. --urlbar-padding-block Block padding of the urlbar. Visual appearance is determined by slotted content, or by the built-in label/description/imageSrc rendering. checked Whether or not the item is selected. disabled Whether or not the item is disabled. itemTabIndex Tabindex of the input element. Only one item is focusable at a time (roving tabindex). name Name of the item, set by the associated moz-visual-picker parent element. value Value of the item. label Visible label for the picker item. description Additional text shown beneath the label. ariaLabel Value for the aria-label attribute. title Native title tooltip. Set labelPosition="outside" when you want the whole row, not just the image, to be clickable via a real label element. Listen for the real input/change events for selection handling, the item isn't backed by a native input and manually dispatches both on selection. Don't set title expecting a normal HTML tooltip, it's mapped onto the inner shadow-DOM item and removed from the host element itself. Don't manage itemTabIndex yourself, it's a roving-tabindex pattern the parent moz-visual-picker controls so only one item is ever focusable at a time; setting it manually will fight the parent's own management. moz-visual-picker-item.border.color moz-visual-picker-item.border.radius.@base moz-visual-picker-item.border.width.@base moz-visual-picker-item.border.width.checked

visual-picker.title: visual-picker
visual-picker.text: A container that groups related moz-visual-picker-item children and allows a user to navigate between them to select one item. Propagates to moz-visual-picker-item children. value Selected value for the group. Changing the value updates the checked state of moz-visual-picker-item children and vice versa. orientation Layout orientation of the picker, "horizontal" (default) or "vertical". Propagates to moz-visual-picker-item children. (default) The picker's content, intended for moz-visual-picker-item children. change Bubbles up from a selected child item; the picker updates its value accordingly. fieldset The wrapping <fieldset>, inherited from SelectControlBaseElement. Call .focus()/.click()/.blur() directly on moz-visual-picker-item, they're overridden to delegate into the inner shadow DOM button (itemEl) rather than acting on the light DOM host.
